true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the exact same bug: in the list view, the 'Silence notifications' menu item is rendered based on promRule abilities, and clicking it sets `showSilenceDrawer`. However, the `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` only renders if the optional ruler rule is present, which is not passed in the list view, making the silence button a no-op.

false_positives.candidate:
Delete never appears in the ruler-less list view

AlertRuleMenu now ORs Grafana Prometheus-rule abilities into canDelete so the list can authorize actions without a ruler fetch. The Delete item is still rendered only when rulerRule is set (`canDelete && rulerRule` at line 165). The new list (GrafanaRuleListItem → RuleActionsButtons) passes only promRule, so rulerRule is undefined and Delete is never shown, even for users with folder delete permission. The list click handler already ignores the ruler argument and opens the delete modal with the identifier built from the Prometheus rule uid, so this guard drops a primary action rather than protecting anything. GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx grants AlertingRuleDelete, defines a delete menu query, and then asserts exactly four menu items, so the regression stays green.

Pause/resume is unreachable without a ruler rule

The Pause item is still rendered only when rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) is true, and MenuItemPauseRule is given that ruler rule. The new list never loads a ruler rule, so canPause computed from useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities is ignored. Users cannot pause or resume rules from the list, including rules whose paused state is already shown from the Prometheus payload (isPaused). MenuItemPauseRule still needs a RulerGrafanaRuleDTO to call the pause API, so the prom-rule ability check cannot drive the action until pause is implemented from the rule uid or the ruler rule is loaded on demand.

Federated rules are no longer immutable

useAllAlertRuleAbilities used to set isFederated from isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) and fold that into immutableRule, which blocks Update, Delete, Pause, Restore, and DeletePermanently. That body now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which only receives a RulerRuleDTO and RuleGroupIdentifierV2 (neither has source_tenants) and hardcodes isFederated to false. Every existing caller of useAlertRuleAbility / useAllAlertRuleAbilities — rule detail and the old rules table, not only the new list — will offer edit and delete on federated Mimir/GEM rules. Those mutations were blocked because saving the group without source_tenants can drop cross-tenant evaluation. The CombinedRule path still has rule.group and should keep the check even if the ruler-only hook cannot.

skipToken still grants Duplicate via Grafana create permission

useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(skipToken) is meant to skip the check for non-Grafana rules, but it calls useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined). For a missing rule, useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable returns loading: false, so MaybeSupported becomes AlwaysSupported, and Duplicate is [true, user has getRulesPermissions('grafana').create]. AlertRuleMenu ORs that with the ruler result. On a cloud/datasource rule, a user who cannot duplicate external rules but can create Grafana-managed rules still sees Duplicate, and choosing it starts RedirectToCloneRule for that cloud rule. skipToken/undefined should be not-supported and not-allowed for every action. The OR also means any false allow on the prom side overrides a ruler denial.

Recording rules lose export and pause in prom abilities

useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities uses prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule as the Grafana-managed check for ModifyExport, Pause, Restore, and DeletePermanently. Recording rules are Grafana-managed too (uid, folderUid, isPaused, provenance on the shared prom DTO). The ruler abilities this replaces used rulerRuleType.grafana.rule, which is true for recording rules, so the old list offered Export and Pause. The new list will not, while Edit and Delete are not gated this way. Silence should stay alerting-only; export, pause, restore, and permanent delete should follow "is a Grafana prom rule" plus the immutability checks, not alerting type.

Rule view links drop returnTo

The removed GrafanaRuleLoader built the view href with createReturnTo() so rule detail could navigate back to the current list URL, including filters and pagination. GrafanaRuleListItem now links to /alerting/grafana/${uid}/view with no returnTo query. Opening a rule from the filtered list and going back lands on the default list instead of the filtered results.

$__range queries are split after interpolation removes the guard

runSplitQuery now runs datasource.applyTemplateVariables before querySupportsSplitting. Grafana puts __range, __range_s, and __range_ms on request.scopedVars from the full dashboard/Explore range, and applyTemplateVariables sends the expression through templateSrv.replace, so those tokens are already gone when isQueryWithRangeVariable runs. The guard therefore never matches, and queries that the comment says must not be split are partitioned into day-sized chunks. Previously the raw expression still contained $__range, so the query was one request and the backend interpolated the macro against the original range. After this change a common metric such as rate({app="foo"}[$__range]) over 30 days becomes rate({app="foo"}[30d]) executed as ~30 one-day requests, each with a 30-day lookback. That multiplies bytes scanned by roughly the chunk count and turns queries that used to succeed into timeouts, limit errors, or aborted splits (shouldStop on the first failed chunk). Decide splitting from the original expression, keep $__range queries in the non-splitting group (they can still be interpolated so other variables resolve), and add a test that such a query calls runQuery once.

$__auto is still expanded per chunk; the new test stubs it away

The early interpolation only calls applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters) and does not inject an __auto value. $__auto is not a Grafana scoped macro ($__interval and $__range are); this file already notes that step handling lives in the backend (pkg/tsdb/loki/step.go) and is only replicated here for chunk boundaries. applyTemplateVariables also cannot compute it: that API receives no time range or intervalMs. Split sub-requests therefore still contain literal $__auto, and the backend substitutes a step derived from each chunk's shorter range, so chunks get different range vectors and the merged series do not match an unsplit query. The new "Interpolates queries before execution" test hides this by replacing templateSrv.replace with a function that unconditionally rewrites $__auto to 5m, which production replace will not do. Substitute $__auto from the original request range (using the same calculateStep result used to partition) before splitting, and assert the executed expression without stubbing that replacement.

Shard path applies template variables twice, duplicating ad-hoc filters

runShardSplitQuery now interpolates every target with applyTemplateVariables, then splitQueriesByStreamShard always executes those targets through runSplitQuery, which applies applyTemplateVariables again after interpolateShardingSelector has rewritten the LogQL to inject __stream_shard__. For one target and four shard groups that is five substitutions; the updated test locks this in by expecting applyTemplateVariables toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5), where it previously expected a single interpolateVariablesInQueries call. The second call is not a no-op: it is passed request.filters again, so ad-hoc matchers are inserted into an expression that already has them, and the executed query looks like {app="foo", env="prod", __stream_shard__=~"1|2", env="prod"}. A second templateSrv.replace pass can also rewrite $... text that the first substitution or the shard rewrite introduced. Interpolate once, before shard grouping and selector lookup, and skip the new interpolation inside runSplitQuery when the caller already did it.

Blank expressions are no longer dropped after interpolation

The empty-expression filter now runs on the raw target, before applyTemplateVariables. The previous shard path interpolated with interpolateVariablesInQueries and only then dropped falsy expr values. A target whose expression is only a variable, such as expr "$logql" resolving to "", used to be removed and is now kept, grouped, and sent to Loki. The parse error is not retriable, so the shard loop sets shouldStop and never runs the remaining groups — one blank interpolated target fails every other query in the request. The same order was introduced in runSplitQuery (querySplitting.ts filters on query.expr and only then maps applyTemplateVariables), with the same abort-the-batch consequence. Filter hidden targets, interpolate, then drop targets whose expression is blank.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The applyTemplateVariables method is called with request.filters as the third parameter, but this parameter is not used in the corresponding test setup.

true_positives.golden_comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Limit check and insert are not atomic

When deviceLimit > 0, CreateOrUpdateDevice runs SELECT COUNT(*) and, if the count is still below the limit, a separate INSERT/upsert on another session. There is no transaction, SELECT FOR UPDATE, advisory lock, or use of the existing server lock around the two steps. Concurrent first-time devices can all observe count < limit and all insert, so the number of rows in the 30-day window can exceed AnonymousDeviceLimit. A burst of new device IDs (restart, many anonymous browsers) will overshoot the configured cap. The count and the write need to be one atomic conditional insert, or held under a lock, so the limit cannot be passed.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the same race condition where concurrent requests can pass the device count check simultaneously and insert devices exceeding the configured limit, and both suggest using a lock or atomic transaction to resolve it.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Device-limit denials are cached as successful tags

tagDeviceUI inserts the device ID into the process-local cache (default TTL about 29 minutes) before CreateOrUpdateDevice returns, and a cache hit returns nil without touching the database. CreateOrUpdateDevice now returns ErrDeviceLimitReached for an unknown device once the cap is hit, and Anonymous.Authenticate treats that error as an authentication failure. The cache entry is not removed on that error, so the next request with the same X-Grafana-Device-Id hits the cache, TagDevice returns success, and a full anonymous identity is issued even though the device was never stored and does not count toward the limit. A second in-flight request can also observe the cache entry while the first call is still in the database and be authenticated before the denial is known. After one rejected attempt, that device ID is allowed for the rest of the TTL, so the new cap does not stop anonymous access. Cache only a successful write, or cache the denial and keep returning ErrDeviceLimitReached.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same bug as the golden comment: `tagDeviceUI` populates the cache before calling `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, and if `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry persists, allowing subsequent requests with the same device ID to bypass the limit for the 29-minute TTL.

false_positives.candidate:
Requests without a device ID skip the cap

The new limit is enforced only when TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached and Authenticate rejects the login. TagDevice returns nil immediately when X-Grafana-Device-Id is empty, and also returns nil when the remote address cannot be parsed as an IP, without reading AnonymousDeviceLimit. Authenticate treats that nil as success and still returns an anonymous identity with the configured org role. Any client that omits the header (API callers, the initial document request before the frontend sets the header, or a client that strips it) is never counted and never rejected. The setting therefore does not cap anonymous access; it only affects clients that voluntarily present a device ID.

Wire providers changed but injector was not updated

ProvideAnonymousDeviceService now takes db.DB instead of anonstore.AnonStore, and ProvideAnonDBStore gained a bare int64 deviceLimit argument. These Provide* functions are constructed by Google Wire; pkg/server/wire.go and the checked-in pkg/server/wire_gen.go are not in this PR. The generated injector still calls the old signatures, so the server package will not compile. Regeneration will also fail if ProvideAnonDBStore remains in the provider set, because Wire cannot tell which int64 should be cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit. Build the store only inside ProvideAnonymousDeviceService, drop ProvideAnonDBStore from the Wire set if nothing else injects AnonStore, and commit the regenerated wire_gen.go.

Anonymous login now blocks on untimed DB tagging

Device tagging used to run in a background goroutine with a 2-minute timeout and could not delay authentication. TagDevice is now called inline on the request context, which has no dedicated deadline, before an anonymous identity is returned. Every cache miss waits for an upsert, and when device_limit is set it also waits for COUNT(*) on anon_device (rows are retained for 61 days). A slow, locked, or unreachable database stalls anonymous authentication for those requests instead of bounding the tag. Put a short timeout around the call and define the timeout outcome so a database problem cannot hang anonymous traffic.

device_limit is an undocumented ini key

auth.anonymous.device_limit is a new operator-facing setting, defaulting to 0 via MustInt64(0). The store only enforces the cap when the value is greater than 0, so 0 means unlimited, not "allow no devices". conf/defaults.ini and the configure-grafana docs are not updated, so the key, its default, and that meaning are undiscoverable. Add it, with that comment, under [auth.anonymous] in defaults.ini and next to the other anonymous auth options.

Limit tests never cover allow-existing or auth

TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks that a second new device ID returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. It does not check that a device already inside the 30-day window is still updated and allowed when the count is at the limit, which is the updateDevice path every returning user depends on. No test calls TagDevice or Anonymous.Authenticate with a non-zero limit, so a local-cache hit that turns a limit error into a successful anonymous login, or a missing X-Grafana-Device-Id that skips the cap, would not fail CI. Add a store test for the at-limit refresh of an existing device and a service test that a new device is denied on every attempt while an already-counted one still authenticates.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.
The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.

Time window calculation inconsistency: Using device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration) as the lower bound but device.UpdatedAt as the current time may not match the intended logic. Consider using time.Now().UTC() consistently.

false_positives.candidate:
Fallback locale YAML is never loaded outside set_locale

The new fallback chain (requested locale, then SiteSetting.default_locale, then :en) only works if those locale files have been loaded into the backend. On-demand loading still only calls load_locale for I18n.config.locale inside I18n.translate, and the new I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! is invoked only from ApplicationController#set_locale. Processes that never hit that filter — Sidekiq workers, mailers, rake tasks, the console — therefore never load the site-default or English YAML. A job that does I18n.with_locale(user.effective_locale) and translates will load only that user's locale; missing keys will not fall back to the site language or English even though the yml files define them. Calls with an explicit locale: option have the same gap, because translate preloads config.locale rather than the locale actually being resolved. Argument-less I18n.t results are also frozen into the 300-entry LRU. The default i18n missing-translation handler returns a "translation missing: ..." string, so one early lookup in a job process caches that string and later lookups never retry after a locale file is loaded. Fallback loading has to happen on the translate path for the locale being resolved, not only in the controller filter.

Translation LRU key ignores the fallback locale

Argument-less translations are cached under "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}" only. This change makes the resolved string also depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, because a key missing from the current locale is filled from the site default (then English) and that resolved string is what gets stored. default_locale is an admin setting that updates in-process without a restart, and nothing here includes the fallback locale in the cache key or clears @cache when it changes (I18n.reload! would clear it, but setting updates do not call that). Hot no-arg keys stay in the 300-entry LRU indefinitely, so after the default locale changes, users missing those keys keep seeing strings from the previous default locale until the worker is restarted.

No coverage for fallback order or on-demand loading

The custom chain [requested locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en] and the ensure_loaded! hook ship with no specs. Nothing asserts that a missing key resolves to the site locale before English, that the fallback YAML is actually loaded before lookup, or that translations outside ApplicationController#set_locale (jobs, mailers, I18n.with_locale) fall back at all. Those non-request paths are exactly where fallback files are not loaded, so the failure would not be caught before merge.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

true_positives.golden_comment: The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. During a refactoring, the tracing import and the logic to extract and add traceID from the context to log parameters were removed from the LoggerMiddleware. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.

That parameter was removed and not replaced: ContextualLoggerMiddleware only stores endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, and uname via log.WithContextualAttributes, and plugins/log.FromContext does not add a trace id before Info. Info itself is not context-aware, so this call site no longer records the trace. Egress logs can no longer be correlated with the request trace (including unsampled traces, which the old false argument included). Put traceID back on the log params, or add the same TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false) value to the contextual attributes.

GET /groups/:name/members JSON shape changed from an array to an object

members used to render_serialized an array of GroupUserSerializer objects, which the old client mapped directly. It now returns {members, meta: {total, limit, offset}} and always paginates (default 50). The in-repo Group model was updated, but any other client, plugin, or cached script that still expects a JSON array will throw when it calls .map (or will only see the first page if it adapts). This is an unversioned break of a public group endpoint; old and new payloads are not accepted together.

Add and remove member failures are silent, and the add field is never cleared

addMembers() ignores the promise from model.addMembers(), and removeMember() ignores removeMember()'s promise. There is no error callback, so a 422, 500, or network failure closes the dialog or clicks Add and leaves the list unchanged with no alert. On success the username field is not cleared (the TODO on the previous line), and findMembers() only reloads the current offset, so a new user who sorts onto another page never appears. The server also returns 200 when every username is unknown (add_members skips failed lookups and still saves), so a typo is indistinguishable from success. Admins cannot tell whether membership changed.

Member page changes race and can display the wrong page

next and previous update group.offset and call findMembers() with no in-flight guard, and the links stay clickable until the response updates showingFirst/showingLast. Two quick clicks issue overlapping requests. findMembers() writes members, user_count, and offset from whichever response settles last, not from the latest offset. A slower request for an earlier page can overwrite a later one, so the pager and the member list disagree until another navigation. The same pattern applies to previous().

Update does not strip group names, and create does not sync the stripped name back

create saves (params[:name] || '').strip, but the client only applies resp.basic_group.id and keeps the raw name (including leading/trailing spaces). update then does group.name = params[:name] with no strip. The admin list therefore shows the unstripped name after create. The next Save posts that raw name; the placeholder says names cannot contain spaces, so validation fails and the rest of the edit is discarded, or a spaced name is stored even though create had already normalized it. Apply the serialized name after create and strip on update the same way as create.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Match stats written during validation are rolled back or double-counted

should_block? increments match_count and last_match_at and calls save while User email validation is running. User#save wraps validation in a transaction that Rails rolls back when save returns false, and a nested BlockedEmail save joins that transaction. On paths that only call save or save! (User.create_for_email and any other creator), a blocked address fails validation and the statistic update is rolled back, so the attempt is never recorded. UsersController#create makes the count path-dependent: it always calls user.valid? first, outside a transaction, which commits one increment, then user.save validates again. If the address is blocked, the second increment is rolled back (net +1). If action_type is do_nothing and the user is otherwise valid, both increments commit (net +2 per signup). save's false return is also ignored, so a failed stat write is silent. Record the match with an explicitly committed atomic update after the allow/block decision, not as a side effect of validation.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the exact same underlying architectural flaw: the `should_block_email?` / `should_block?` check method has database write side effects (updating match statistics) during a read/validation operation. The candidate goes into deeper detail about the specific transaction rollback and double-counting bugs caused by this side effect in Rails.

true_positives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Domain allow/deny regex is unanchored and barely escaped

email_in_restriction_setting? builds a case-insensitive regexp of @(domain-list) after only replacing dots with backslash-dot, and the pattern is not anchored at the end of the address. A whitelist of company.com therefore matches user@company.com.attacker.example, and that signup is allowed. That defeats email_domains_whitelist as an access control: any host that merely starts with an allowed domain plus a dot is treated as allowed. The same prefix match makes a blacklist of spam.com also reject user@spam.com.legitimate.example. Only dots are escaped before interpolation, so a setting value that contains other regexp metacharacters (an unmatched parenthesis, +, *) either matches the wrong addresses or raises RegexpError during validation and 500s every signup and email change. This was moved unchanged from User#email_validator. Escape each domain and anchor the match at a domain boundary and at the end of the string before relying on these settings.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the same vulnerability in the `email_in_restriction_setting?` method: the regex `@(#{domains})` lacks proper boundary anchoring, allowing an attacker to bypass the domain whitelist using a specially crafted domain (note: the candidate correctly explains the exploit as `company.com.attacker.example` since `@` anchors the start of the domain, while the golden comment says `evil.example.com`, both refer to the exact same unanchored regex bug).

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocklist lookup is case-sensitive and not normalized

should_block? loads BlockedEmail.where(email: email) with the raw address, and nothing downcases or strips email before the uniqueness validation or insert. The rest of this app already normalizes addresses with Email.downcase and strip (UsersController#change_email, User.find_by_username_or_email), and the domain allow/deny regex is case-insensitive, but this blocklist is an exact match. PostgreSQL's unique index on blocked_emails.email is case-sensitive as well, so Spam@evil.com and spam@evil.com are different rows. A blocked address such as spam@evil.com can register by changing case or adding surrounding whitespace; the client rejectedEmails list has the same exact-string hole because it stores and compares result.values.email unchanged. Normalize with Email.downcase and strip in a before_validation callback and again inside should_block? before the query, so the block cannot be bypassed and case-variants cannot both be inserted.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the exact same vulnerability: the email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` is case-sensitive, which allows blocked users to bypass the blocklist simply by changing the casing of their email address.

false_positives.candidate:
BlockedEmail.actions calls Enum with the wrong constructor

BlockedEmail.actions does Enum.new(:block, :do_nothing). Enum in this application (lib/enum.rb) takes a single hash of name => stable integer, the same form used by every other enum (for example PostActionType). Passing two symbols raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments). actions is invoked from set_defaults on every BlockedEmail save, from should_block? once a matching row is loaded (both record.save's before_validation and the action_type comparison), and from the fabricator, where action_type BlockedEmail.actions[:block] is evaluated when fabricators load. Blocked emails cannot be created through ActiveRecord, the new specs error, and if a row is inserted another way any signup whose email matches that row 500s inside validation instead of returning the blocked-email error. Define it as Enum.new(:block => 1, :do_nothing => 2) so stored action_type values are explicit and do not change if symbols are reordered.

match_count update is a lost-update race

The counter is updated by reading match_count, adding 1 in memory, and calling save, with no row lock and no atomic SQL increment. Two concurrent signups that both load the same blocked_emails row each write old+1, so one attempt is dropped; last_match_at can also be overwritten by the slower request. A burst of registrations against one blocked address silently undercounts. Use a single UPDATE ... SET match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ? WHERE id = ? (or increment_counter) so concurrent matches are not lost.

Block and domain checks are stubbed away, so the new rules are untested

The validator spec stubs BlockedEmail.should_block? and only asserts that some email error is present or absent. It never checks that the message is user.email.blocked, never exercises email_domains_whitelist or email_domains_blacklist (so the unanchored-domain bypass stays green), and never runs User validations, so a broken validates :email, email: true wiring would still pass. blocked_email_spec only looks up the exact casing it inserted, so Spam@evil.com bypassing a spam@evil.com block is not caught, and nothing asserts match_count across UsersController#create's valid?-then-save path. There is also no example that a failed create returns errors and values, which the signup UI now depends on. Those cases need real records, not stubs.

Every email error is cached as a permanent format failure

On a failed create, the client pushObjects result.values.email whenever result.errors.email is set. That key is present for every email validation failure (already taken, domain not allowed, or blocked), not only blocklist hits. emailValidation then fails that exact string with I18n.t('user.email.invalid') — the same copy used for a malformed address — and submit stays disabled until the address text changes. The flash is the only place the real server reason appears; afterward the field says the address is invalid, and it cannot be resubmitted even if the failure was transient or the conflicting account is removed. rejectedEmails is also a prototype Em.A([]) and is never cleared when the modal closes, so the rejection sticks for the life of the page. Only cache blocklist rejections, or show the server's error string, and do not reuse the format-invalid translation.

true_positives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Small-action button no longer stays on the right edge

.small-action is now a flex row (flexbox() and align-items(center) at the top of the rule), but its delete/recover button is still only positioned with float: right. Float does not apply to flex items, so a direct-child button (the usual Discourse small-action markup: avatar, description, then the times button) stays in source order instead of pinning to the row's right edge. Even if the button is nested in .small-action-desc, that description is a default flex item (flex: 0 1 auto, no flex-grow) and now has only padding: 0 1.5% instead of a full-width block with 4em left padding, so a float inside it aligns to the text, not the far side of the post. The X that used to sit at the right of closed/pinned/similar action rows now sits immediately beside the action text and is easy to mis-click next to the username. Browsers that ignore flexbox still honor .topic-avatar { float: left }, and the 4em padding that kept the description clear of that 45px icon is gone, so the text runs through the icon. Give the description flex: 1 and min-width: 0, put margin-left: auto and flex-shrink: 0 on the button, and stop using float for either child.
true_positives.reasoning: The golden comment encompasses two issues: 1) mixing float: left with flexbox (which occurs in .small-action .topic-avatar) and 2) removing float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel. The candidate issue accurately identifies the first part of the golden comment regarding mixing float and flexbox in .small-action, explaining the resulting layout bugs in detail.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
order mixin writes 0-based values into 1-based box-ordinal-group

@mixin order($val) copies $val unchanged onto -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group as well as the modern order property. The 2009 box-ordinal-group property is 1-based and defaults to 1; modern order is 0-based and defaults to 0. Those prefixed declarations therefore do not implement order (the usual fix, used by Autoprefixer, is $val + 1). order(0) emits an invalid box-ordinal-group: 0, and order(1) ties with unordered siblings instead of coming after them. The new call sites pass 2 and 3 (.d-header .panel and .extra-info-wrapper), which still sort after the default group, so those two values happen to keep the same sequence in old WebKit/Firefox — but the shared mixin is wrong for every other value and should not be merged as the compatibility layer.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue point out the exact same problem: `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` are 1-based properties, whereas the `order` mixin directly copies the 0-based `$val` without adjusting it (e.g., when `$val` is 0).

false_positives.candidate:
Header panel right-alignment has no working legacy fallback

.d-header .panel was float: right and .d-header .title was float: left. Both floats were removed and the panel is now only pushed right with margin-left: auto, while .contents is a flex container via the new flexbox() mixin. Auto main-axis margins absorb free space only in the 2012+ flex model (display: flex / -webkit-flex / -ms-flexbox). flexbox() also emits display: -webkit-box. Browsers that honor that 2009 value and not the later display values (stock Android 4.1–4.3, older iOS) lay the header out as an old horizontal box: floats on the flex items are ignored and margin-left: auto does not push, so the logo and the icon/login cluster sit together on the left. Browsers with no flexbox at all ignore every display value in the mixin; margin-left: auto on a block with width: auto computes to 0, so title and panel stack as full-width blocks. Theme CSS that still right-aligns .panel with float stops working for the same reason. Do not emit 2009 display values unless a 2009 spacer (-webkit-box-flex) actually pins the panel, and keep the float rules as the non-flex fallback.

false_negatives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
website_name bypasses anonymous TL0 website hiding

website_name is computed from the profile website, but it is not subject to the same anonymous trust-level-0 restriction as website. untrusted_attributes only defines include_<attr>? for bio, location, website, and the background fields, and that guard is what stops anonymous viewers (and crawlers hitting /users/:username.json) from seeing a new user's website. The new include_website_name method is never called: this serializer, like ActiveModel Serializers 0.8, only invokes include_website_name? (question mark), which is how every other include hook in this file is named. Even if it were renamed, it only returns website.present? and never calls scope.restrict_user_fields?(object). Previously the client derived the label from model.website, so when website was omitted the globe link disappeared. Now an anonymous profile request for a TL0 user omits website but still receives website_name (host, and host+path when the comparison matches), and the template renders it. That restores the spam-visible website the restriction exists to hide. Put :website_name in untrusted_attributes and delete this include method; a later include_website_name? that only checks website.present? would override the macro and keep the leak. As written, users with a blank website also always get "website_name": null, because the include hook does not run.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue explicitly identifies the primary bug from the golden comment: that `include_website_name` is missing the required `?` suffix (`include_website_name?`), which causes the conditional inclusion hook in ActiveModel Serializers to never be called. While the candidate does not mention the secondary string concatenation issue and elaborates further on the security implications of the broken hook, it accurately captures the core serializer method naming bug.

false_positives.candidate:
Same-domain check mis-classifies hosts

website_name's host comparison does not match "same domain", so the path is added for unrelated sites and omitted for equivalent ones. Equality and ends_with? are case-sensitive, but Ruby's URI parser keeps host case and Discourse.current_hostname is lowercase: http://Example.com/user on a forum at example.com fails every branch and displays Example.com with no path. The sibling branch (same label count > 2, then compare everything after the first label) treats evil.co.uk and forum.co.uk, or a.github.io and b.github.io, as the same site because the shared suffix is a public suffix, and appends the path. The else branch's discourse_host.ends_with?("." + website_host) is true for any suffix, so a website host of com matches every *.com forum and the label becomes com plus the path. The parent check is one-way: example.com on a www.example.com forum includes the path, but http://www.example.com/user on an example.com forum does not, because the label counts differ and example.com does not end with .www.example.com. Profile labels will therefore show paths for unrelated domains and hide paths for the same site entered with different case or a www prefix.

Displayed website name drops non-default ports

website_name keeps only URI#host, which never includes the port, then optionally appends the path. The removed client label used website.split("/")[2], so http://example.com:8443/app was shown as example.com:8443. It is now shown as example.com when the host is unrelated, or example.com/app when the host comparison matches. The href is still the original URL, but the visible text identifies the default port. Any profile website on a non-default port is mislabeled, including links that are not on the forum domain.

Specs miss the TL0 leak and domain edge cases

The anonymous TL0 example still only asserts that bio, location, website, and background keys are absent, and it never sets a website. website_name is therefore free to appear in that JSON (as a host/path, or as null when the include hook does not run) without failing the suite. The new examples only stub current_hostname to discourse.org, example.com, and forums.example.com against an already-lowercased http://example.com/user, so they do not catch case-sensitive misses, port stripping, the www child case, or false matches such as another *.co.uk host or a website host of com. Those are the paths that produce the wrong label or the privacy leak, and the added specs still pass if they ship.

true_positives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feed URL is passed to Kernel#open with no scheme check

poll_feed passes SiteSetting.feed_polling_url directly to open() after requiring open-uri. Nothing checks that the setting is an http or https URL. In Ruby, open('|...') spawns a shell and open('/path') reads a local file; open-uri only special-cases strings that look like URLs. A feed setting of a pipe command or filesystem path (admin UI, API, or script running as an admin) becomes command execution or local file read on the next poll. http URLs are also fetched with no timeout, redirect allowlist, or response size limit, so a slow or huge feed blocks a worker and can exhaust memory.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the same vulnerability: passing the unvalidated `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url` directly to `open()` in the `PollFeed` job, which leads to SSRF, local file read, or command execution.

true_positives.golden_comment: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Resize postMessage uses the full referer as targetOrigin

The embed layout calls parent.postMessage(message, request.referer). The second argument must be an origin (scheme://host[:port]), but request.referer is a full URL with path and query. Browsers then throw or drop the message (target origin does not match the parent). ERB escaping also turns `&` in the referer into `&`, so the string would not match even without a path. embed.js only grows the iframe from that discourse-resize message and sets scrolling=no, so comments stay clipped at the default iframe height.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue accurately identifies the exact same bug described in the golden comment: passing the full referrer URL instead of the origin as the targetOrigin in postMessage, which causes the message to be dropped and prevents iframe resizing.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Imported HTML is stored and rendered without sanitization

Post#cook returns the raw body unchanged when cook_method is raw_html, and TopicEmbed.import saves remote HTML with that cook method (skip_validations: true). PollFeed (poll_feed.rb:35) runs CGI.unescapeHTML on the feed body first, which turns escaped tags back into real markup, and never runs Sanitize. import_remote only whitelists a few tags/attributes and still allows javascript: href/src values. TopicEmbed.import also interpolates the source URL, unescaped, into an href (topic_embed.rb:13). Cooked HTML is treated as trusted in the forum UI, and best.html.erb:19 emits it with `raw`. A feed item or imported page can therefore store script or javascript: links that execute in the Discourse origin for every viewer of the topic or embed.
true_positives.reasoning: The golden comment identifies two issues in TopicEmbed.import: a NoMethodError when contents is nil, and an XSS vulnerability from unescaped URL interpolation into HTML. The candidate issue explicitly points out one of these exact concerns: 'TopicEmbed.import also interpolates the source URL, unescaped, into an href (topic_embed.rb:13)', identifying the same XSS vulnerability.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Embed template has a Ruby syntax error and cannot render

best.html.erb closes its first conditional with `<%- end if %>` (line 6). That compiles to `end if`, which is a Ruby syntax error, so ActionView raises when an existing embed topic is rendered and the iframe gets a 500. The new controller spec never renders views, so it still passes. On-demand and feed-imported embeds cannot display comments until this is a plain `end`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the exact same syntax error in the ERB template: closing an if block with `end if` instead of `end`, which causes a Ruby syntax error upon rendering.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feed poll crashes on typical RSS items

poll_feed always calls i.content.scrub and CGI.unescapeHTML. SimpleRSS exposes standard RSS 2.0 bodies as description (and content:encoded as content_encoded), not content, so i.content is missing or nil and this raises NoMethodError. String#scrub itself only exists on Ruby 2.1+, so the same line crashes on Ruby 1.9/2.0 even when content is present. There is no per-item rescue, and the job sets retry: false, so one bad item aborts the rest of that hourly import. Titles and links are also used unchecked, so a blank title fails the same way.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the same bug: calling `i.content.scrub` will raise a NoMethodError (nil pointer exception) when `i.content` is nil, which happens frequently in standard RSS feeds that use `description` instead of `content`.

false_positives.candidate:
Public embed endpoint triggers unbounded server-side fetches

EmbedController#best is an unauthenticated GET. Its only gate is that the Referer host equals embeddable_host (embed_controller.rb:26), which any non-browser client can spoof. It then enqueues RetrieveTopic for the caller-supplied embed_url (embed_controller.rb:15). TopicRetriever only compares URI#host to that setting and does not restrict scheme or port (topic_retriever.rb:15). import_remote then calls open(url).read with no timeout or size cap. open-uri follows redirects, so a path on the configured host that 302s to a link-local or internal URL is fetched from the Discourse server, and the body is loaded entirely into memory. Distinct embed_urls each enqueue work, so this is also a job-queue and memory DoS, and a successful HTML response is imported as a topic posted by embed_by_username.

Loading embed never reliably advances to the topic

When no TopicEmbed exists, EmbedController renders loading and then calls discourse_expires_in 1.minute (embed_controller.rb:19), marking that response cacheable. The loading page reloads itself after 30 seconds via location.reload() with no cache-busting flag, so the browser may reuse the fresh cached loading document and never notice that the topic was created. If the reload does hit the server, authorization still requires the Referer host to be embeddable_host. A reload's Referer is often the iframe's own Discourse URL or empty, not the original parent page, so ensure_embeddable returns InvalidAccess and the iframe stays on the error or loading state.

Host-spam check still blocks imports for a new embed user

TopicEmbed.import creates the topic with skip_validations: true, but PostCreator still runs rollback_if_host_spam_detected before save. has_host_spam? is skipped only for trust level basic and above, and newuser_spam_host_threshold defaults to 3. A newly created embed_by_username account is trust level 0, and imported HTML usually contains several links to the same host, so the create transaction is rolled back. import still treats the returned post object as present and TopicEmbed.create! then fails on a null post_id. Feed polling and on-demand retrieve both fail for ordinary articles unless the configured user is already TL1+.

embed_url is limited to 255 characters

embed_url is a Rails string column, created as varchar(255), with a unique index on that column. Article and tracking URLs often exceed 255 characters. PostgreSQL then raises a string-truncation error, the import transaction rolls back, and that page can never be embedded. There is no foreign key or dependent: :destroy on topic_id/post_id either, so deleting the topic leaves a topic_embeds row; topic_id_for_embed still returns the dead id, TopicView errors, and TopicRetriever skips the URL because the row exists, so the embed never heals.

Protocol-relative URLs are rewritten onto the article host

absolutize_urls treats every href and src that starts with `/` as a root-relative path and strips leading slashes before prefixing the article origin. Protocol-relative URLs such as //cdn.example.com/img.png start with `/`, so they become http://article-host/cdn.example.com/img.png. Relative links that do not start with `/` (img.png, ../img.png) are left untouched. Imported RSS and readability HTML commonly uses both forms, so images and links in the created topic are broken. The port logic also drops the port whenever it is 80 or 443, so https on port 80 or http on port 443 is rewritten to the wrong default port.

Retrieve throttle can lock a URL forever

retrieved_recently? claims the per-URL lock with SETNX and only then sets a 60 second TTL in a second command. If the process dies between those calls, retrieved:<url> is left with no expiry. Later retrieves treat the URL as recently fetched forever, unless the viewer is staff (no_throttle). The key is also set before a successful fetch, so a crash or a failed fetch in that window permanently prevents import of that embed URL. SET with NX and EX in one command would avoid the stuck key.

Every embed miss synchronously imports the entire feed

On a cache miss, perform_retrieve calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute inline before fetching the requested URL. That downloads the whole feed and runs TopicEmbed.import for every item, inside the RetrieveTopic worker that was enqueued just to import one page. One iframe view can occupy a Sidekiq thread for the full feed and create or revise every feed topic. The redis lock only lasts 60 seconds, so a slow poll overlaps the next retrieve and starts another full import. The scheduled job already polls hourly; this path should not repeat that work synchronously.

Disqus import now requires live fetches and drops category and dates

The importer used to create a local permalink topic with the XML thread's created_at and an optional --category. It now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote for t[:link] and the category option was removed, so every thread is fetched over HTTP, posted as the current time, and lands in the default category. import_remote is not rescued: one missing link, non-http link, timeout, or readability failure raises and aborts the rest of the export. The task can no longer import from the XML file alone.

Embeddable host comparison is case-sensitive

invalid_host? and EmbedController#ensure_embeddable compare SiteSetting.embeddable_host to URI#host with != and do not downcase either side. Hostnames are case-insensitive, but Ruby's URI#host keeps the original case, so a referer or embed_url of http://EvilTrout.com is rejected when the setting is eviltrout.com. The embed then 403s or never imports even though the host is the configured one.

Poll feed specs do not exercise the guards they name

The examples that claim execute requires feed_polling_url and embed_by_username never stub feed_polling_enabled? to true. That setting defaults to false, so execute returns before those checks and the examples pass even if the url or username guard is deleted. Nothing calls poll_feed, so nil content, non-http item links, Kernel#open behavior, and TopicEmbed.import failures are untested. The embed controller spec also does not render views, which is why the best.html.erb syntax error is invisible to CI.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.

Input and output are the same path. The false return value is ignored, so Upload.create_for on line 72 stores the damaged file. The path is also the wrong file identity. Even if the path ended in .gif, gifsicle --resize-fit (optimized_image.rb:120) expects pixel geometry such as 100x100, not ImageMagick's 80%, so that branch would fail too. true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Missing TopicUser 500s, and save! does not record an explicit choice

unsubscribe does TopicUser.find_by and immediately reads tu.notification_level. If the logged-in viewer has no topic_users row (the URL is not bound to the email recipient; any logged-in user who can see the topic can open it), tu is nil and this raises NoMethodError. tu.save! also bypasses TopicUser.change, which is what sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed, sets notifications_changed_at, creates a missing row, and publishes /topic/:id on MessageBus. The mailer creates the recipient row with TopicUser.change(last_emailed_post_number:) and does not set a reason, so reason often stays nil. update_last_read then auto-upgrades notification_level back to tracking when notifications_reason_id is null and view time exceeds the auto-track threshold, and TopicUser.auto_track does the same when reason is nil. true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue explicitly identifies the exact same nil pointer exception (NoMethodError) when no TopicUser record exists and `tu` is nil, while also providing additional context on how to properly fix it using `TopicUser.change`.

false_positives.candidate:
render :show runs before canonical_url is set

perform_show_response now calls render :show inside the HTML branch (topics_controller.rb:500). TopicsController#show only calls canonical_url after perform_show_response returns (line 87). Previously the HTML branch did not render, so Rails implicit render ran after the action finished and the layout still saw @canonical_url. render evaluates the show template and layout immediately, so @canonical_url is still nil and every topic HTML response loses its canonical link. This is a silent site-wide regression, not limited to unsubscribe. Move the render back out of the shared method, or set the canonical URL before rendering.

Unsubscribe mutates notification state on a cookie-authenticated GET

config/routes.rb registers topics#unsubscribe as GET (t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and t/:topic_id/unsubscribe), and the action writes TopicUser.notification_level at topics_controller.rb:107-113 with no per-user token. Topic#unsubscribe_url (topic.rb:719) is only /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe, the same for every recipient, unlike the existing digest link email/unsubscribe/:key. Rails forgery protection does not cover GET, so any page can include that URL as an image or link and, for a logged-in victim, downgrade or mute the topic. Email prefetchers and link scanners that send the user's cookies will do the same without a click. Logged-out recipients are only redirected to login, so the link does not identify or unsubscribe the person who was emailed. The Ember route never calls an unsubscribe API; it only loads the topic. A safe design is a signed, user-specific token, or a GET confirmation page plus a POST that uses TopicUser.change.

Unsubscribe does not stop notifications for watchers and is not idempotent

If notification_level is above regular (tracking=2 or watching=3), unsubscribe sets regular (1); otherwise it sets muted (0). Watching is what causes an email on every new post, and the new copy promises a full stop: server.en.yml unsubscribe_link says "stop receiving notifications about this particular topic", and client.en.yml topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications says "You will stop receiving notifications". After one request those users are still at regular, so replies, mentions, and quotes still notify. The transition is also not idempotent: a second GET (refresh, duplicate fetch, or a scanner request plus the user's click) sees regular and mutes. Outcome depends on how many times the URL is hit, and mute hides the topic from the user's lists, which is stronger than stopping email and is never explained. Always set muted (or another single terminal level) through TopicUser.change, and make repeat requests a no-op.

Unsubscribe template name does not match the route

The route is registered as topicUnsubscribe at /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe (app-route-map.js.es6:13). The new controller, route, and view are all topic-unsubscribe, which Ember resolves as topicUnsubscribe / template topic-unsubscribe. This template lives at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which compiles to the name topic/unsubscribe (nested route topic.unsubscribe). No code renders that name, and there is no templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs. The view also does not set templateName. After the Rails shell loads, the confirmation screen is blank: the stop-notifications copy and topic-notifications-button never appear, so the user cannot see or correct the level the GET just wrote. Move the template to templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs, or nest the route under topic and move the controller and view to match.

The only test change passes unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe" so I18n can interpolate unsubscribe_link. The example at line 179 still only checks that the user-preferences URL is in the body; it never asserts the per-topic URL or the new "click here" sentence. There is no request/controller spec for TopicsController#unsubscribe: missing TopicUser, watching versus regular, a second GET, slug redirect, logged-out access, or CSRF. The broken level transitions and the nil TopicUser crash can ship without a failing test.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:

If a fixed host has no entry for that weekday, every callback is falsy, find returns undefined, and the slot is kept. That is the round-robin case this PR is meant to close: union slots from a rotating host stay bookable on days the fixed host does not work. true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

A full-day block is stored as an override whose start equals its end, and this callback tries to reject the whole day in that case. The comparison uses === on two dayjs objects, which is reference equality and is never true, so that branch never runs. The following checks only mark a slot outside a window when the slot ends at or before the override start or starts strictly after the override end. A slot that merely overlaps the window — starts before it, ends after it, or straddles a zero-length block — is treated as inside. find() then stops at the first same-day range that does not contain the slot, so two override ranges on one day (a normal custom-hours override with a gap) reject a slot that sits inside the other range and the day shows no bookable override slots. The date match also uses only the adjusted start, so an override whose UTC interval crosses midnight does not cover slots on the second day. false_positives.candidate:
Slots inside a date override skip busy checks and can double-book

checkIfIsAvailable now returns true as soon as a slot falls on a day with a date override and is treated as inside that override, before the busy-interval scan. That scan is the only place calendar conflicts and existing Cal bookings are applied to generated slots, and this function now runs for every fixed host — including ordinary personal and collective events, whose users are marked isFixed. On any day that has a date override, a slot inside the override is therefore shown as free even when the host is already booked, so the same time can be booked twice.

Override date match compares server-local date to UTC date

Whether an override applies to a slot is decided by formatting the offset-adjusted start with a local-mode dayjs and comparing it to slotStartTime.format(), and slotStartTime is in UTC mode (time.utc()). format() on a local-mode instance uses the process timezone, not UTC. Whenever the server timezone is not UTC, the two calendar dates disagree for overrides near midnight and the override is applied to the wrong day or not applied at all, so fixed-host date overrides silently fail outside a UTC process.

Timezone-adjusted overrides drop the day and can wipe that day's hours

Override start/end are converted by adding the invitee-minus-organizer offset and then keeping only hour and minute. That throws away a day boundary. If the shift moves one end across midnight and not the other, endTime is less than startTime; buildSlots discards any range with start >= end. The caller has already deleted that user's normal working hours for the invitee day the raw UTC timestamp fell on, so the day is left with no slots. Even when both ends wrap to clock times on the same side of midnight, the activeOverrides filter (line 206) still selects the invitee day that contains the unadjusted timestamp, whose UTC clock is the organizer wall time rather than the real instant. For a non-zero organizer offset those are different instants, so an evening override viewed from a timezone ahead (US host, European booker) is attached to the wrong calendar day. The new +6 test only shifts IST 14:00–18:00 by 30 minutes and stays on the same day, so it does not catch this.

Already-adjusted override minutes are DST-shifted again in buildSlots

The new override minutes are computed from the override date's own organizer and invitee offsets, so they are already invitee-local minutes for that date. They are then pushed into computedLocalAvailability and passed through buildSlots, which adds organizerDSTDiff - inviteeDSTDiff. That correction exists for working hours converted with today's offset (dayjs.tz(dayjs(), timeZone)), not for values already adjusted to the target date. When today and the booking day sit on different sides of a DST transition and the invitee timezone does not have the same delta, override slots move by an hour. Asia/Kolkata and Asia/Dhaka do not observe DST, so the added test cannot see it.

false_positives.candidate:
Any two errors permanently drop in-window SMS reminders

Every thrown error in the scheduling try, and every falsy scheduleSMS result, increments the same retryCount, and the next cron deletes the row once retryCount > 1. That includes transient failures (Twilio 5xx or rate limits, getBookerBaseUrl, profile lookup), not only permanent ones such as an invalid number. This job loads every unscheduled SMS reminder whose scheduledDate is within 7 days, so two failed ticks during a short outage delete that whole window. Deletion is irreversible and there is no backoff or Twilio error-code check, so those attendees never get the text even after the provider recovers. Count only permanent send failures toward this cap; leave transient errors retryable until the scheduled date.

Missing phone or empty body never hits the retry limit

retryCount is incremented only inside the branch that actually calls scheduleSMS. If sendTo is missing (SMS_ATTENDEE with a null booking.smsReminderNumber, or SMS_NUMBER with an empty step sendTo) or the rendered body is empty, the handler skips the send and leaves retryCount at 0 and scheduled false, as long as nothing earlier threw. Those rows stay in the unscheduled-within-7-days query and are fully reprocessed, including profile and booker-URL lookups, on every cron run until scheduledDate is past — the unbounded retry this change is meant to stop. Missing numbers are a common permanent failure and never reach Twilio, so they never reach the new delete. Increment retryCount or delete the row when there is nothing to send.

Catch-path retry update can abort the cron and orphan a sent SMS

The new catch updates retryCount and does not handle that update failing. The try also wraps the update that stores the Twilio SID after scheduleSMS returns a message. If that SID update throws, the catch still treats it as a scheduling failure: it increments retryCount and leaves scheduled false and referenceId empty even though Twilio already accepted the message. Later runs schedule more messages for the same reminder, and once retryCount > 1 the row is deleted, so none of those messages can be cancelled. Separately, if the catch update itself throws (Prisma P2025 when a concurrent run already deleted the row), the error escapes the catch, the for-loop stops, and every later reminder in the batch is skipped. Previously this catch only logged. Guard the retry update, and do not count a failure that happens after Twilio has already returned a message as 'not scheduled'.

OR retryCount delete cannot use the existing reminder index

deleteMany now ORs an unindexed retryCount > 1 predicate with the scheduledDate predicate. WorkflowReminder's index is (method, scheduled, scheduledDate) and was not extended for retryCount in the schema change. An OR against a column with no index typically forces a sequential scan of the whole table on every cron tick, taking row locks for deleted tuples, including email and WhatsApp reminders this job does not own. Split the two cleanups into separate deletes and add an index that matches the retry predicate so this cron does not scan the full reminder table.

No tests for retry accounting or the delete predicate

This change deletes workflow reminders and adds no tests. Coverage needs to lock the intended contract: scheduleSMS returning null increments retryCount; a thrown error increments it; the row is removed only after retryCount exceeds 1 and only for unscheduled SMS; a successful schedule with a stored referenceId is not deleted; a missing phone or empty body does not remain in the cron until the event time. Without that, the unscoped deleteMany and the silent no-send path will not be caught before they drop reminders in production.

Ungrouped OR fragments break AND composition and can skip authorization

Team and org authorization SQL is an OR of two branches with no surrounding parenthesis group: ("teamId" = … AND "isTeamBooking" = true) OR ("userId" = ANY(…) AND "isTeamBooking" = false), built at the reduce in buildOrgAuthorizationCondition (line 173) and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition (line 204). The event-type filter is the same shape: ("eventTypeId" = $id) OR ("eventParentId" = $id) at line 106, also returned without an outer group when it is the only filter. getBaseConditions wraps each side only when both auth and filters are present (line 73). With no service filters it returns the bare authorization fragment here. That is the common insights path: this service only filters eventTypeId and memberUserId, and findMany (which AND-merged arbitrary caller where-clauses inside Prisma, so grouping was safe) was removed. Callers must add the time window themselves. WHERE ${getBaseConditions()} AND "startTime" >= $from AND "status" = 'accepted' is parsed as (team branch) OR (personal branch AND startTime >= $from AND status = 'accepted') because AND binds tighter than OR. Every team booking for that team is included regardless of date or status, so team/org insights over-count and ignore caller predicates. A second composition, WHERE ${getAuthorizationConditions()} AND ${getFilterConditions()}, is the obvious translation of the old findMany AND and is also wrong: it parses as (auth AND eventTypeId = $id) OR eventParentId = $id, so any booking whose eventParentId matches is returned even when it fails the org/team/user authorization predicate. That leaks rows for child/managed event types outside the caller's scope. Wrap every returned fragment, including the final OR and this no-filter return, in parentheses (Prisma.sql`(${fragment})`) before it is embedded. The new tests expect the unparenthesized text, so they lock the unsafe shape in.

Team/org SQL is never executed; toEqual does not match nested Prisma.sql

The team-scope assertion here, the org-scope assertion around line 332, and the combined-filter assertion around line 429 compare getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions to a single flat Prisma.sql template via toEqual. Those service methods build the predicate with Array.reduce, so the returned Prisma.Sql values array holds nested Sql fragments; flattening happens only when a query is executed, not in the constructor. vitest deep-equality compares that structure, not rendered SQL, so these three tests fail even when the SQL text matches. NOTHING, user-scope, and single-filter cases are flat templates and can pass, which hides the failure mode. The only query actually sent to the database is the user-scope getBaseConditions case (line 481), which is a pure AND and does not use OR or ANY(array). A passing run therefore does not check team/org authorization, array binding for ANY(${ids}), or the operator-precedence bug when these fragments are AND-ed with a date or status predicate. Execute the team and org fragments with $queryRaw (including an extra AND predicate) and assert both included and excluded rows.

scheduleEmailReminders begins by deleteMany-ing every EMAIL WorkflowReminder whose scheduledDate is at or before now, and only afterward loads cancelled=true rows to POST a SendGrid cancel. With the job running every 15 minutes, a cancellation made after the last tick before scheduledDate (or any run that starts at or after the send time, including a delayed cron) always hits this path. The new cancel query cannot see those rows because they are already gone. SendGrid withdrawal for cancelled=true reminders has to run before this cleanup, and the cleanup must not delete cancelled rows that have not yet been cancelled at SendGrid.

The new cancel loop awaits every SendGrid POST inside a single try/catch, and only after the whole loop does it await the queued workflowReminder.delete calls. Prisma queries are lazy, so those deletes have not run yet. If any request throws (unknown or already-cancelled batch id, the pending-cancellation cap, a network error), the catch only logs and then the handler goes on to schedule other mail. This handler explicitly allows attendees, and the booker is an attendee while booking.userId is the host, so the booker path — a primary use of "add guests" — does not have those credential ids. The same happens for a team admin acting on someone else's booking, and even the owner path only has one user's credentials, so other collective hosts' calendar references are skipped. Guests can be stored while the existing invites still list the old attendees.

Only the email call is in try/catch, and that catch logs a fixed string, drops the error object, and then the handler still returns success. Newly added guests are stored as attendees, so anyone with a Cal.com account for that address can invite more people. This is an authedProcedure, not limited to the bookings page.

For event types with seatsPerTimeSlot, occupancy is tracked with BookingSeat rows tied to attendees. This update only createManys Attendee records. It never creates BookingSeat rows and never compares the result to seatsPerTimeSlot (that value is only copied onto the calendar payload at line 145). The disable handler in apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts line 61 does the same. Uppercase letters, spaces, or a different dash fail the match and are reported as an incorrect code.
