true_positives.golden_comment: The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
New members pagination and admin member routes are untested at the HTTP layer

GroupsController#members changed from a full (or 200-row) array to a paginated {members, meta} object, and there is no spec for the default limit, offset, total, or response shape, so the public 50-member truncation would not fail CI. Admin add_members/remove_member specs call the actions directly with group_id and never go through config/routes.rb. A member route that supplies :id instead of :group_id, or a path that does not match /admin/groups/:id/members, would 400/404 in the browser while these specs stay green. The automatic remove example even uses xhr :put against an action routed as DELETE.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly identifies the route supplying :id while the actions expect :group_id, causing HTTP requests to fail despite direct-action tests passing. Although framed as a test-coverage concern and bundled with other issues, it captures the same parameter mismatch and broken membership access.

false_positives.candidate:
Public group members list is capped at 50 with no pagination

The public group members route now calls Group.findMembers(), which always requests limit 50 (Discourse.Group default, and GroupsController#members defaults to 50 and always applies limit/offset). The members template only renders that page and has no next/previous or load-more control, unlike the new admin UI. Non-automatic groups previously returned every member, and automatic groups previously returned up to 200. Groups larger than 50 now look complete while everyone after the first page is omitted, with no indication of the total.

Creating a group drops the selected alias level

The new-group form shows the alias-level combo (it is outside the {{#if id}} block) and Group.asJSON posts alias_level, but Admin::GroupsController#create only assigns name and visible before save. alias_level stays at the database default (0 / nobody) no matter what the admin picked. The client only copies basic_group.id from the response, so the form still shows the unsaved choice until a full reload. A second Save happens to persist it via update, but leaving the page or refreshing loses the setting. Update already honors alias_level; create does not, and the create spec only checks name stripping.

Removing the last member on a page leaves a blank page

removeMember reloads via findMembers() without moving offset backward. findMembers clamps offset with the pre-delete user_count (Math.min(user_count, offset)), so an offset already on the last page is kept. The server echoes that offset even when it is past the new end (GroupsController#members does not clamp). Example: 51 members, limit 50, page 2 shows one user; after that user is removed the request still uses offset 50, the response is an empty list with total 50, and the admin stays on an empty page until they click Previous.

Group update treats a missing visible flag as false and ignores the old payload

update always does group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" and reads name/alias_level from top-level params. The previous API (and any cached admin JS, plugin, or script) sent a nested group hash and could PATCH incremental membership changes. Those requests no longer include top-level visible, so this saves visible=false and returns 200, hiding the group, while name, alias_level, and usernames in group[...] are ignored and PATCH add/remove is gone. A missing or old-format update therefore persists a visibility change the caller did not make. Reject the old shape or read both params[:visible] and params[:group], and do not default visibility to false when the key is absent.

GET /groups/:name/members JSON shape changed from an array to an object

members used to render_serialized an array of GroupUserSerializer objects, which the old client mapped directly. It now returns {members, meta: {total, limit, offset}} and always paginates (default 50). The in-repo Group model was updated, but any other client, plugin, or cached script that still expects a JSON array will throw when it calls .map (or will only see the first page if it adapts). This is an unversioned break of a public group endpoint; old and new payloads are not accepted together.

Add and remove member failures are silent, and the add field is never cleared

addMembers() ignores the promise from model.addMembers(), and removeMember() ignores removeMember()'s promise. There is no error callback, so a 422, 500, or network failure closes the dialog or clicks Add and leaves the list unchanged with no alert. On success the username field is not cleared (the TODO on the previous line), and findMembers() only reloads the current offset, so a new user who sorts onto another page never appears. The server also returns 200 when every username is unknown (add_members skips failed lookups and still saves), so a typo is indistinguishable from success. Admins cannot tell whether membership changed.

Member page changes race and can display the wrong page

next and previous update group.offset and call findMembers() with no in-flight guard, and the links stay clickable until the response updates showingFirst/showingLast. Two quick clicks issue overlapping requests. findMembers() writes members, user_count, and offset from whichever response settles last, not from the latest offset. A slower request for an earlier page can overwrite a later one, so the pager and the member list disagree until another navigation. The same pattern applies to previous().

Update does not strip group names, and create does not sync the stripped name back

create saves (params[:name] || '').strip, but the client only applies resp.basic_group.id and keeps the raw name (including leading/trailing spaces). update then does group.name = params[:name] with no strip. The admin list therefore shows the unstripped name after create. The next Save posts that raw name; the placeholder says names cannot contain spaces, so validation fails and the rest of the edit is discarded, or a spaced name is stored even though create had already normalized it. Apply the serialized name after create and strip on update the same way as create.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Match stats written during validation are rolled back or double-counted

should_block? increments match_count and last_match_at and calls save while User email validation is running. User#save wraps validation in a transaction that Rails rolls back when save returns false, and a nested BlockedEmail save joins that transaction. On paths that only call save or save! (User.create_for_email and any other creator), a blocked address fails validation and the statistic update is rolled back, so the attempt is never recorded. UsersController#create makes the count path-dependent: it always calls user.valid? first, outside a transaction, which commits one increment, then user.save validates again. If the address is blocked, the second increment is rolled back (net +1). If action_type is do_nothing and the user is otherwise valid, both increments commit (net +2 per signup). save's false return is also ignored, so a failed stat write is silent. Record the match with an explicitly committed atomic update after the allow/block decision, not as a side effect of validation.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify statistics updates as an inappropriate side effect of the should-block check. The candidate details transaction rollback and double-counting consequences rather than emphasizing race conditions and misleading naming, but the underlying concern is the same.

true_positives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Domain allow/deny regex is unanchored and barely escaped

email_in_restriction_setting? builds a case-insensitive regexp of @(domain-list) after only replacing dots with backslash-dot, and the pattern is not anchored at the end of the address. A whitelist of company.com therefore matches user@company.com.attacker.example, and that signup is allowed. That defeats email_domains_whitelist as an access control: any host that merely starts with an allowed domain plus a dot is treated as allowed. The same prefix match makes a blacklist of spam.com also reject user@spam.com.legitimate.example. Only dots are escaped before interpolation, so a setting value that contains other regexp metacharacters (an unmatched parenthesis, +, *) either matches the wrong addresses or raises RegexpError during validation and 500s every signup and email change. This was moved unchanged from User#email_validator. Escape each domain and anchor the match at a domain boundary and at the end of the string before relying on these settings.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify improper domain-boundary anchoring in the regex built by email_in_restriction_setting?, allowing unintended domains to match whitelist entries. The candidate uses a different bypass example and adds escaping concerns, but identifies the same underlying regex validation issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocklist lookup is case-sensitive and not normalized

should_block? loads BlockedEmail.where(email: email) with the raw address, and nothing downcases or strips email before the uniqueness validation or insert. The rest of this app already normalizes addresses with Email.downcase and strip (UsersController#change_email, User.find_by_username_or_email), and the domain allow/deny regex is case-insensitive, but this blocklist is an exact match. PostgreSQL's unique index on blocked_emails.email is case-sensitive as well, so Spam@evil.com and spam@evil.com are different rows. A blocked address such as spam@evil.com can register by changing case or adding surrounding whitespace; the client rejectedEmails list has the same exact-string hole because it stores and compares result.values.email unchanged. Normalize with Email.downcase and strip in a before_validation callback and again inside should_block? before the query, so the block cannot be bypassed and case-variants cannot both be inserted.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same case-sensitive email lookup in BlockedEmail.should_block? and explains that changing an email's capitalization bypasses the block. Its additional whitespace and normalization concerns do not change the core match.

false_positives.candidate:
BlockedEmail.actions calls Enum with the wrong constructor

BlockedEmail.actions does Enum.new(:block, :do_nothing). Enum in this application (lib/enum.rb) takes a single hash of name => stable integer, the same form used by every other enum (for example PostActionType). Passing two symbols raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments). actions is invoked from set_defaults on every BlockedEmail save, from should_block? once a matching row is loaded (both record.save's before_validation and the action_type comparison), and from the fabricator, where action_type BlockedEmail.actions[:block] is evaluated when fabricators load. Blocked emails cannot be created through ActiveRecord, the new specs error, and if a row is inserted another way any signup whose email matches that row 500s inside validation instead of returning the blocked-email error. Define it as Enum.new(:block => 1, :do_nothing => 2) so stored action_type values are explicit and do not change if symbols are reordered.

match_count update is a lost-update race

The counter is updated by reading match_count, adding 1 in memory, and calling save, with no row lock and no atomic SQL increment. Two concurrent signups that both load the same blocked_emails row each write old+1, so one attempt is dropped; last_match_at can also be overwritten by the slower request. A burst of registrations against one blocked address silently undercounts. Use a single UPDATE ... SET match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ? WHERE id = ? (or increment_counter) so concurrent matches are not lost.

Block and domain checks are stubbed away, so the new rules are untested

The validator spec stubs BlockedEmail.should_block? and only asserts that some email error is present or absent. It never checks that the message is user.email.blocked, never exercises email_domains_whitelist or email_domains_blacklist (so the unanchored-domain bypass stays green), and never runs User validations, so a broken validates :email, email: true wiring would still pass. blocked_email_spec only looks up the exact casing it inserted, so Spam@evil.com bypassing a spam@evil.com block is not caught, and nothing asserts match_count across UsersController#create's valid?-then-save path. There is also no example that a failed create returns errors and values, which the signup UI now depends on. Those cases need real records, not stubs.

Every email error is cached as a permanent format failure

On a failed create, the client pushObjects result.values.email whenever result.errors.email is set. That key is present for every email validation failure (already taken, domain not allowed, or blocked), not only blocklist hits. emailValidation then fails that exact string with I18n.t('user.email.invalid') — the same copy used for a malformed address — and submit stays disabled until the address text changes. The flash is the only place the real server reason appears; afterward the field says the address is invalid, and it cannot be resubmitted even if the failure was transient or the conflicting account is removed. rejectedEmails is also a prototype Em.A([]) and is never cleared when the modal closes, so the rejection sticks for the life of the page. Only cache blocklist rejections, or show the server's error string, and do not reuse the format-invalid translation.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
order mixin writes 0-based values into 1-based box-ordinal-group

@mixin order($val) copies $val unchanged onto -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group as well as the modern order property. The 2009 box-ordinal-group property is 1-based and defaults to 1; modern order is 0-based and defaults to 0. Those prefixed declarations therefore do not implement order (the usual fix, used by Autoprefixer, is $val + 1). order(0) emits an invalid box-ordinal-group: 0, and order(1) ties with unordered siblings instead of coming after them. The new call sites pass 2 and 3 (.d-header .panel and .extra-info-wrapper), which still sort after the default group, so those two values happen to keep the same sequence in old WebKit/Firefox — but the shared mixin is wrong for every other value and should not be merged as the compatibility layer.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: the order mixin passes 0-based values unchanged to -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group, which require values starting at 1, making order(0) invalid and causing legacy-browser layout issues.

false_positives.candidate:
Small-action button no longer stays on the right edge

.small-action is now a flex row (flexbox() and align-items(center) at the top of the rule), but its delete/recover button is still only positioned with float: right. Float does not apply to flex items, so a direct-child button (the usual Discourse small-action markup: avatar, description, then the times button) stays in source order instead of pinning to the row's right edge. Even if the button is nested in .small-action-desc, that description is a default flex item (flex: 0 1 auto, no flex-grow) and now has only padding: 0 1.5% instead of a full-width block with 4em left padding, so a float inside it aligns to the text, not the far side of the post. The X that used to sit at the right of closed/pinned/similar action rows now sits immediately beside the action text and is easy to mis-click next to the username. Browsers that ignore flexbox still honor .topic-avatar { float: left }, and the 4em padding that kept the description clear of that 45px icon is gone, so the text runs through the icon. Give the description flex: 1 and min-width: 0, put margin-left: auto and flex-shrink: 0 on the button, and stop using float for either child.

Header panel right-alignment has no working legacy fallback

.d-header .panel was float: right and .d-header .title was float: left. Both floats were removed and the panel is now only pushed right with margin-left: auto, while .contents is a flex container via the new flexbox() mixin. Auto main-axis margins absorb free space only in the 2012+ flex model (display: flex / -webkit-flex / -ms-flexbox). flexbox() also emits display: -webkit-box. Browsers that honor that 2009 value and not the later display values (stock Android 4.1–4.3, older iOS) lay the header out as an old horizontal box: floats on the flex items are ignored and margin-left: auto does not push, so the logo and the icon/login cluster sit together on the left. Browsers with no flexbox at all ignore every display value in the mixin; margin-left: auto on a block with width: auto computes to 0, so title and panel stack as full-width blocks. Theme CSS that still right-aligns .panel with float stops working for the same reason. Do not emit 2009 display values unless a 2009 spacer (-webkit-box-flex) actually pins the panel, and keep the float rules as the non-flex fallback.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
website_name bypasses anonymous TL0 website hiding

website_name is computed from the profile website, but it is not subject to the same anonymous trust-level-0 restriction as website. untrusted_attributes only defines include_<attr>? for bio, location, website, and the background fields, and that guard is what stops anonymous viewers (and crawlers hitting /users/:username.json) from seeing a new user's website. The new include_website_name method is never called: this serializer, like ActiveModel Serializers 0.8, only invokes include_website_name? (question mark), which is how every other include hook in this file is named. Even if it were renamed, it only returns website.present? and never calls scope.restrict_user_fields?(object). Previously the client derived the label from model.website, so when website was omitted the globe link disappeared. Now an anonymous profile request for a TL0 user omits website but still receives website_name (host, and host+path when the comparison matches), and the template renders it. That restores the spam-visible website the restriction exists to hide. Put :website_name in untrusted_attributes and delete this include method; a later include_website_name? that only checks website.present? would override the macro and keep the leak. As written, users with a blank website also always get "website_name": null, because the include hook does not run.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly identifies the missing '?' suffix on include_website_name and explains that the serializer therefore never invokes the conditional inclusion hook. This matches the golden comment's primary issue, although the candidate does not mention the string-literal mutation concern and additionally discusses privacy implications.

false_positives.candidate:
Same-domain check mis-classifies hosts

website_name's host comparison does not match "same domain", so the path is added for unrelated sites and omitted for equivalent ones. Equality and ends_with? are case-sensitive, but Ruby's URI parser keeps host case and Discourse.current_hostname is lowercase: http://Example.com/user on a forum at example.com fails every branch and displays Example.com with no path. The sibling branch (same label count > 2, then compare everything after the first label) treats evil.co.uk and forum.co.uk, or a.github.io and b.github.io, as the same site because the shared suffix is a public suffix, and appends the path. The else branch's discourse_host.ends_with?("." + website_host) is true for any suffix, so a website host of com matches every *.com forum and the label becomes com plus the path. The parent check is one-way: example.com on a www.example.com forum includes the path, but http://www.example.com/user on an example.com forum does not, because the label counts differ and example.com does not end with .www.example.com. Profile labels will therefore show paths for unrelated domains and hide paths for the same site entered with different case or a www prefix.

Displayed website name drops non-default ports

website_name keeps only URI#host, which never includes the port, then optionally appends the path. The removed client label used website.split("/")[2], so http://example.com:8443/app was shown as example.com:8443. It is now shown as example.com when the host is unrelated, or example.com/app when the host comparison matches. The href is still the original URL, but the visible text identifies the default port. Any profile website on a non-default port is mislabeled, including links that are not on the forum domain.

Specs miss the TL0 leak and domain edge cases

The anonymous TL0 example still only asserts that bio, location, website, and background keys are absent, and it never sets a website. website_name is therefore free to appear in that JSON (as a host/path, or as null when the include hook does not run) without failing the suite. The new examples only stub current_hostname to discourse.org, example.com, and forums.example.com against an already-lowercased http://example.com/user, so they do not catch case-sensitive misses, port stripping, the www child case, or false matches such as another *.co.uk host or a website host of com. Those are the paths that produce the wrong label or the privacy leak, and the added specs still pass if they ship.

true_positives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feed URL is passed to Kernel#open with no scheme check

poll_feed passes SiteSetting.feed_polling_url directly to open() after requiring open-uri. Nothing checks that the setting is an http or https URL. In Ruby, open('|...') spawns a shell and open('/path') reads a local file; open-uri only special-cases strings that look like URLs. A feed setting of a pipe command or filesystem path (admin UI, API, or script running as an admin) becomes command execution or local file read on the next poll. http URLs are also fetched with no timeout, redirect allowlist, or response size limit, so a slow or huge feed blocks a worker and can exhaust memory.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the direct use of SiteSetting.feed_polling_url in open() without URL validation. The candidate emphasizes command execution, local file access, and resource exhaustion rather than SSRF, but points to the same unsafe input handling at the same call site.

true_positives.golden_comment: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Resize postMessage uses the full referer as targetOrigin

The embed layout calls parent.postMessage(message, request.referer). The second argument must be an origin (scheme://host[:port]), but request.referer is a full URL with path and query. Browsers then throw or drop the message (target origin does not match the parent). ERB escaping also turns `&` in the referer into `&`, so the string would not match even without a path. embed.js only grows the iframe from that discourse-resize message and sets scrolling=no, so comments stay clipped at the default iframe height.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: passing the full referrer URL as postMessage's targetOrigin instead of only the origin, causing resize messages to fail and preventing iframe resizing.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Imported HTML is stored and rendered without sanitization

Post#cook returns the raw body unchanged when cook_method is raw_html, and TopicEmbed.import saves remote HTML with that cook method (skip_validations: true). PollFeed (poll_feed.rb:35) runs CGI.unescapeHTML on the feed body first, which turns escaped tags back into real markup, and never runs Sanitize. import_remote only whitelists a few tags/attributes and still allows javascript: href/src values. TopicEmbed.import also interpolates the source URL, unescaped, into an href (topic_embed.rb:13). Cooked HTML is treated as trusted in the forum UI, and best.html.erb:19 emits it with `raw`. true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

false_positives.candidate:
Public embed endpoint triggers unbounded server-side fetches

EmbedController#best is an unauthenticated GET. Its only gate is that the Referer host equals embeddable_host (embed_controller.rb:26), which any non-browser client can spoof. It then enqueues RetrieveTopic for the caller-supplied embed_url (embed_controller.rb:15). TopicRetriever only compares URI#host to that setting and does not restrict scheme or port (topic_retriever.rb:15). import_remote then calls open(url).read with no timeout or size cap. open-uri follows redirects, so a path on the configured host that 302s to a link-local or internal URL is fetched from the Discourse server, and the body is loaded entirely into memory. Distinct embed_urls each enqueue work, so this is also a job-queue and memory DoS, and a successful HTML response is imported as a topic posted by embed_by_username.

Loading embed never reliably advances to the topic

When no TopicEmbed exists, EmbedController renders loading and then calls discourse_expires_in 1.minute (embed_controller.rb:19), marking that response cacheable. The loading page reloads itself after 30 seconds via location.reload() with no cache-busting flag, so the browser may reuse the fresh cached loading document and never notice that the topic was created. If the reload does hit the server, authorization still requires the Referer host to be embeddable_host. A reload's Referer is often the iframe's own Discourse URL or empty, not the original parent page, so ensure_embeddable returns InvalidAccess and the iframe stays on the error or loading state.

Host-spam check still blocks imports for a new embed user

TopicEmbed.import creates the topic with skip_validations: true, but PostCreator still runs rollback_if_host_spam_detected before save. has_host_spam? is skipped only for trust level basic and above, and newuser_spam_host_threshold defaults to 3. A newly created embed_by_username account is trust level 0, and imported HTML usually contains several links to the same host, so the create transaction is rolled back. import still treats the returned post object as present and TopicEmbed.create! then fails on a null post_id. Feed polling and on-demand retrieve both fail for ordinary articles unless the configured user is already TL1+.

embed_url is limited to 255 characters

embed_url is a Rails string column, created as varchar(255), with a unique index on that column. Article and tracking URLs often exceed 255 characters. PostgreSQL then raises a string-truncation error, the import transaction rolls back, and that page can never be embedded. There is no foreign key or dependent: :destroy on topic_id/post_id either, so deleting the topic leaves a topic_embeds row; topic_id_for_embed still returns the dead id, TopicView errors, and TopicRetriever skips the URL because the row exists, so the embed never heals.

Protocol-relative URLs are rewritten onto the article host

absolutize_urls treats every href and src that starts with `/` as a root-relative path and strips leading slashes before prefixing the article origin. Protocol-relative URLs such as //cdn.example.com/img.png start with `/`, so they become http://article-host/cdn.example.com/img.png. Relative links that do not start with `/` (img.png, ../img.png) are left untouched. Imported RSS and readability HTML commonly uses both forms, so images and links in the created topic are broken. The port logic also drops the port whenever it is 80 or 443, so https on port 80 or http on port 443 is rewritten to the wrong default port.

Retrieve throttle can lock a URL forever

retrieved_recently? claims the per-URL lock with SETNX and only then sets a 60 second TTL in a second command. If the process dies between those calls, retrieved:<url> is left with no expiry. Later retrieves treat the URL as recently fetched forever, unless the viewer is staff (no_throttle). The key is also set before a successful fetch, so a crash or a failed fetch in that window permanently prevents import of that embed URL. SET with NX and EX in one command would avoid the stuck key.

Every embed miss synchronously imports the entire feed

On a cache miss, perform_retrieve calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute inline before fetching the requested URL. That downloads the whole feed and runs TopicEmbed.import for every item, inside the RetrieveTopic worker that was enqueued just to import one page. One iframe view can occupy a Sidekiq thread for the full feed and create or revise every feed topic. The redis lock only lasts 60 seconds, so a slow poll overlaps the next retrieve and starts another full import. The scheduled job already polls hourly; this path should not repeat that work synchronously.

Disqus import now requires live fetches and drops category and dates

The importer used to create a local permalink topic with the XML thread's created_at and an optional --category. It now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote for t[:link] and the category option was removed, so every thread is fetched over HTTP, posted as the current time, and lands in the default category. import_remote is not rescued: one missing link, non-http link, timeout, or readability failure raises and aborts the rest of the export. The task can no longer import from the XML file alone.

Embeddable host comparison is case-sensitive

invalid_host? and EmbedController#ensure_embeddable compare SiteSetting.embeddable_host to URI#host with != and do not downcase either side. Hostnames are case-insensitive, but Ruby's URI#host keeps the original case, so a referer or embed_url of http://EvilTrout.com is rejected when the setting is eviltrout.com. The embed then 403s or never imports even though the host is the configured one.

The examples that claim execute requires feed_polling_url and embed_by_username never stub feed_polling_enabled? to true. That setting defaults to false, so execute returns before those checks and the examples pass even if the url or username guard is deleted. Nothing calls poll_feed, so nil content, non-http item links, Kernel#open behavior, and TopicEmbed.import failures are untested. The embed controller spec also does not render views, which is why the best.html.erb syntax error is invisible to CI.

true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same hardcoded 10MB client-side limit replacing per-type site settings, causing divergence from configured upload limits. It also explicitly identifies the repeated hardcoded limit in the HTTP 413 alert, matching the golden comment.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
In-place downsize runs on an extensionless tempfile

create_upload downsizes with OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails) at uploads_controller.rb:67. Input and output are the same path. ImageMagick does not support that: convert can truncate the destination before it finishes reading, leaving a zero-byte or corrupt image, and the original bytes are already overwritten so there is no fallback. The false return value is ignored, so Upload.create_for on line 72 stores the damaged file. The path is also the wrong file identity. Rack multipart tempfiles are named like /tmp/RackMultipart... with no suffix, and the URL download uses the prefix discourse-upload-#{type} rather than the real extension; the original name lives only in filename. ImageMagick picks the output coder from the destination suffix, so the write can fail with no encode delegate or emit bytes that do not match filename and content_type. Animation is dropped for the same reason: OptimizedImage.optimize (optimized_image.rb:155) adds the gifsicle path only when the path matches /\.GIF$/i. An extensionless tempfile never matches, so every oversized GIF goes through convert ...[0], which keeps only the first frame. allow_animated_thumbnails therefore cannot preserve animation. Even if the path ended in .gif, gifsicle --resize-fit (optimized_image.rb:120) expects pixel geometry such as 100x100, not ImageMagick's 80%, so that branch would fail too. Tempfile#size is an fstat of the still-open descriptor; if convert replaces the path by rename, the size loop and the filesize passed to create_for keep seeing the old inode. Downsize into a new tempfile that keeps the original extension, and only replace the upload if the command succeeds and the new file is non-empty.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly identifies that gifsicle --resize-fit expects pixel geometry rather than "80%", causing the animated GIF downsizing branch to fail. This matches the golden issue, despite the candidate also raising other concerns.

false_positives.candidate:
Downsize loop can finish still over the limit

The loop at uploads_controller.rb:66 calls OptimizedImage.downsize up to five times and ignores a false return. convert_with returns false when ImageMagick or gifsicle exits non-zero or ImageOptim raises, and it throws away stderr (&> /dev/null), so a failed pass leaves the file unchanged or truncated while the loop only decrements attempt. It then always calls Upload.create_for with no check that the file is under SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. Each pass is a relative 80% geometry shrink plus another lossy re-encode and ImageOptim run, not a resize aimed at the byte limit. Five passes leave about 33% of the linear dimensions (about 10% of the pixels), which is not enough when the upload is near the new 10MB client ceiling and max_image_size_kb is much smaller. The while condition uses tempfile.size, which will not change if the tool replaced the path and the open descriptor still stats the old inode, so all five attempts run anyway. No tests for downsizing or the new size caps

Nothing covers an image over max_image_size_kb being stored under that limit, convert failing or still being over the limit after five passes, an animated GIF keeping or losing frames, attachments still honoring max_attachment_size_kb, or OptimizedImage.downsize accepting both a geometry string and numeric width/height. true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Missing TopicUser 500s, and save! does not record an explicit choice

unsubscribe does TopicUser.find_by and immediately reads tu.notification_level. If the logged-in viewer has no topic_users row (the URL is not bound to the email recipient; any logged-in user who can see the topic can open it), tu is nil and this raises NoMethodError. tu.save! also bypasses TopicUser.change, which is what sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed, sets notifications_changed_at, creates a missing row, and publishes /topic/:id on MessageBus. The mailer creates the recipient row with TopicUser.change(last_emailed_post_number:) and does not set a reason, so reason often stays nil. update_last_read then auto-upgrades notification_level back to tracking when notifications_reason_id is null and view time exceeds the auto-track threshold, and TopicUser.auto_track does the same when reason is nil. The unsubscribe can be silently undone on a later visit, and other open tabs are not notified. Use TopicUser.change so a missing row is created and the user's choice is sticky.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly identifies the same nil dereference: TopicUser.find_by can return nil when no record exists, and accessing tu.notification_level then raises NoMethodError. Its additional concerns do not negate this match.

false_positives.candidate:
render :show runs before canonical_url is set

perform_show_response now calls render :show inside the HTML branch (topics_controller.rb:500). TopicsController#show only calls canonical_url after perform_show_response returns (line 87). Previously the HTML branch did not render, so Rails implicit render ran after the action finished and the layout still saw @canonical_url. render evaluates the show template and layout immediately, so @canonical_url is still nil and every topic HTML response loses its canonical link. This is a silent site-wide regression, not limited to unsubscribe. Move the render back out of the shared method, or set the canonical URL before rendering.

Unsubscribe mutates notification state on a cookie-authenticated GET

config/routes.rb registers topics#unsubscribe as GET (t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and t/:topic_id/unsubscribe), and the action writes TopicUser.notification_level at topics_controller.rb:107-113 with no per-user token. Topic#unsubscribe_url (topic.rb:719) is only /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe, the same for every recipient, unlike the existing digest link email/unsubscribe/:key. Rails forgery protection does not cover GET, so any page can include that URL as an image or link and, for a logged-in victim, downgrade or mute the topic. Email prefetchers and link scanners that send the user's cookies will do the same without a click. Logged-out recipients are only redirected to login, so the link does not identify or unsubscribe the person who was emailed. The Ember route never calls an unsubscribe API; it only loads the topic. A safe design is a signed, user-specific token, or a GET confirmation page plus a POST that uses TopicUser.change.

Unsubscribe does not stop notifications for watchers and is not idempotent

If notification_level is above regular (tracking=2 or watching=3), unsubscribe sets regular (1); otherwise it sets muted (0). Watching is what causes an email on every new post, and the new copy promises a full stop: server.en.yml unsubscribe_link says "stop receiving notifications about this particular topic", and client.en.yml topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications says "You will stop receiving notifications". After one request those users are still at regular, so replies, mentions, and quotes still notify. The transition is also not idempotent: a second GET (refresh, duplicate fetch, or a scanner request plus the user's click) sees regular and mutes. Outcome depends on how many times the URL is hit, and mute hides the topic from the user's lists, which is stronger than stopping email and is never explained. Always set muted (or another single terminal level) through TopicUser.change, and make repeat requests a no-op.

Unsubscribe template name does not match the route

The route is registered as topicUnsubscribe at /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe (app-route-map.js.es6:13). The new controller, route, and view are all topic-unsubscribe, which Ember resolves as topicUnsubscribe / template topic-unsubscribe. This template lives at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which compiles to the name topic/unsubscribe (nested route topic.unsubscribe). No code renders that name, and there is no templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs. The view also does not set templateName. After the Rails shell loads, the confirmation screen is blank: the stop-notifications copy and topic-notifications-button never appear, so the user cannot see or correct the level the GET just wrote. Move the template to templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs, or nest the route under topic and move the controller and view to match.

No spec covers unsubscribe behavior or the new email link

The only test change passes unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe" so I18n can interpolate unsubscribe_link. The example at line 179 still only checks that the user-preferences URL is in the body; it never asserts the per-topic URL or the new "click here" sentence. There is no request/controller spec for TopicsController#unsubscribe: missing TopicUser, watching versus regular, a second GET, slug redirect, logged-out access, or CSRF. The broken level transitions and the nil TopicUser crash can ship without a failing test.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime

Split the two cleanups into separate deletes and add an index that matches the retry predicate so this cron does not scan the full reminder table.

This change deletes workflow reminders and adds no tests. Coverage needs to lock the intended contract: scheduleSMS returning null increments retryCount; a thrown error increments it; the row is removed only after retryCount exceeds 1 and only for unscheduled SMS; a successful schedule with a stored referenceId is not deleted; a missing phone or empty body does not remain in the cron until the event time. They now call async deleteScheduledEmailReminder / deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside forEach and never await the promises: handleCancelBooking.ts around the new reminder loop, handleNewBooking.ts reschedule (the try/catch there cannot observe async failures), bookings.tsx requestReschedule, and the workflow update/delete paths in workflows.tsx. For an already-scheduled email, the cancelled=true update inside that floating call is the only signal the cron uses to withdraw the SendGrid batch. For an unscheduled email or SMS (no referenceId), the helper's row delete is the only thing stopping the reminder cron from sending it; scheduleEmailReminders schedules every scheduled=false email inside 72 hours and does not check booking status. On a serverless invocation those promises can be frozen when the handler returns, so the booking is cancelled but the reminder is still sent. The calls have to be awaited, and failures surfaced, before the handler finishes.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same underlying issue: async deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls are not awaited inside forEach loops during booking cancellation/rescheduling and workflow updates/deletions, potentially leaving scheduled reminders active.

true_positives.golden_comment: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

deleteScheduledEmailReminder's immediateDelete branch POSTs /v3/user/scheduled_sends with status cancel and then returns without setting WorkflowReminder.cancelled and without deleting the row. Reschedule in handleNewBooking.ts (the call that passes true), workflow deletion in workflows.tsx, and workflow-step deletion in workflows.tsx all use that branch. That reintroduces the failure this PR describes: each cancel stays in SendGrid's scheduled_sends list until the original send time, and once the pending-cancellation cap (stated as 100) is reached further cancels fail and the email is still sent. Failures are only logged inside the helper, and cancelled is never set, so the new cron cannot retry. Workflow and step deletion then cascade-delete the WorkflowReminder, which also removes any chance of a later retry; a bulk delete of more than 100 already-scheduled reminders therefore silently leaves the overflow emails queued. On reschedule the old booking is not deleted, so the row stays scheduled=true and cancelled=null: if the SendGrid call failed the old reminder is still delivered, and if it succeeded the stale row is only removed when scheduledDate passes.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same immediateDelete branch failing to delete the WorkflowReminder record or mark it cancelled, and using SendGrid's cancellation POST instead of the omitted DELETE call. Its additional discussion of cancellation limits and retry behavior does not change the underlying match.

false_positives.candidate:
Cron deletes due reminders before withdrawing them from SendGrid

scheduleEmailReminders begins by deleteMany-ing every EMAIL WorkflowReminder whose scheduledDate is at or before now, and only afterward loads cancelled=true rows to POST a SendGrid cancel. Any cancelled reminder whose send time has already arrived is removed from the database and never cancelled at SendGrid, so the email is still delivered. With the job running every 15 minutes, a cancellation made after the last tick before scheduledDate (or any run that starts at or after the send time, including a delayed cron) always hits this path. The new cancel query cannot see those rows because they are already gone. SendGrid withdrawal for cancelled=true reminders has to run before this cleanup, and the cleanup must not delete cancelled rows that have not yet been cancelled at SendGrid.

One SendGrid cancel error aborts the batch and drops successful deletes

The new cancel loop awaits every SendGrid POST inside a single try/catch, and only after the whole loop does it await the queued workflowReminder.delete calls. Prisma queries are lazy, so those deletes have not run yet. If any request throws (unknown or already-cancelled batch id, the pending-cancellation cap, a network error), the catch only logs and then the handler goes on to schedule other mail. None of the reminders already cancelled at SendGrid are deleted, and every reminder after the failure is skipped. Those rows stay cancelled=true and are retried on the next run. There is no orderBy and no per-item isolation, so one permanently failing row can be selected first every 15 minutes and block every other cancellation until scheduledDate passes. At that point the opening deleteMany removes the rows without a SendGrid cancel and the emails send. Each reminder needs its own error handling, and a successful cancel must be persisted immediately so it is not retried and cannot poison the queue.

Paid cancellations return before workflow reminders are cancelled

In handleCancelBooking a paid booking is refunded and then returns 'Booking successfully cancelled' before the new reminder-cancellation loop. The booking status is already CANCELLED or REJECTED, but its WorkflowReminder rows are left untouched. Before/after-event workflow emails and SMS for paid bookings are therefore neither marked cancelled, deleted, nor withdrawn from SendGrid/Twilio, which is the same production failure this PR is fixing. The cancellation loop has to run on this path as well, and be awaited, before the early return.

No regression test for deferred cancellation of scheduled reminders

The description says the previous SendGrid cancel fix did not work in production, but this change adds no test for the replacement contract. Nothing asserts that booking cancel sets WorkflowReminder.cancelled instead of POSTing scheduled_sends immediately, that reschedule does not use the immediate SendGrid cancel, that the cron withdraws cancelled batches before deleting past-due rows, or that one failed cancel is retried without dropping the rest of the batch. Those are the paths that still send reminders for cancelled and rescheduled bookings, and they will regress silently without a test.

false_positives.candidate:
Calendar update uses the actor's credentials, not the host's

The query loads booking.user with credentials and destinationCalendar, but updateCalendarAttendees is called with an EventManager built from ctx.user and getUsersCredentials(ctx.user). Calendar references store the host credential id. This handler explicitly allows attendees, and the booker is an attendee while booking.userId is the host, so the booker path — a primary use of "add guests" — does not have those credential ids. The host calendar event is then not updated (or the call throws). The same happens for a team admin acting on someone else's booking, and even the owner path only has one user's credentials, so other collective hosts' calendar references are skipped. Guests can be stored while the existing invites still list the old attendees.

Attendees are committed before calendar and email, with no recovery

prisma.booking.update createMany commits the new Attendee rows before updateCalendarAttendees and sendAddGuestsEmails. Only the email call is in try/catch, and that catch logs a fixed string, drops the error object, and then the handler still returns success. If the calendar update throws (wrong credentials, provider error), the mutation 500s after the rows exist, emails never run, and AddGuestsDialog does not invalidate the bookings query on error. A retry treats those addresses as already invited and throws emails_must_be_unique_valid, so the guests stay on the booking with no mail and no calendar update, and the user cannot retry. There is no compensation or idempotent resend.

Attendees can fan out meeting invites with no state or guest limits

The only gate is organizer, attendee email match, or the broken team-admin check. booking.status and endTime are never read, so guests can be added to CANCELLED, REJECTED, PENDING, and already-ended bookings. The new mailers always attach an ICS with status CONFIRMED (attendee-add-guests-email.ts line 15, organizer-add-guests-email.ts line 19) and the payload includes the video URL from booking references, so a pending or cancelled meeting's join link is emailed as a confirmed invite. eventType.disableGuests is never read, so this bypasses the public booking form's no-guests setting. ZAddGuestsInputSchema.guests (addGuests.schema.ts line 5) is an unbounded email array, and each new address gets AttendeeScheduledEmail. Newly added guests are stored as attendees, so anyone with a Cal.com account for that address can invite more people. This is an authedProcedure, not limited to the bookings page.

Seated bookings get bare Attendee rows with no seat check

For event types with seatsPerTimeSlot, occupancy is tracked with BookingSeat rows tied to attendees. This update only createManys Attendee records. It never creates BookingSeat rows and never compares the result to seatsPerTimeSlot (that value is only copied onto the calendar payload at line 145). Seat counts and the attendee list diverge: availability that counts seats will ignore these people, while the bookings UI and the add-guest emails include them. seatsShowAttendees is not enforced before the full attendee list is emailed. Paid seated events can also gain people who never took or paid for a seat.

Add guests is shown for past bookings

The new additional_guests action is pushed into editBookingActions, which is nested in bookedActions. bookedActions is not only rendered for upcoming confirmed bookings; it is also rendered for past confirmed bookings (line 554) and past pending bookings (line 553). Those rows can open AddGuestsDialog and call addGuests. Combined with the handler not rejecting ended bookings, that sends confirmation mail and calendar updates for a meeting that already happened. The action should be limited to upcoming accepted bookings.

No tests for the new addGuests mutation

The PR adds an authenticated mutation that writes attendees, updates calendars, and sends mail, and it adds no tests. There is no coverage for the admin/owner/organizer/attendee/stranger matrix, blacklist and case-insensitive dedup, booking status and disableGuests, seated events, or the branch that chooses AttendeeScheduledEmail versus AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. The admin/owner condition is already wrong; a handler test with an admin who is not the host would have failed the merge.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup-code match is case-sensitive and only strips hyphens

Stored codes are lowercase hex from randomBytes(5).toString("hex"), but login compares credentials.backupCode with indexOf after replaceAll("-", "") only. The disable handler in apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts line 61 does the same. Uppercase letters, spaces, or a different dash fail the match and are reported as an incorrect code. The field placeholder is XXXXX-XXXXX, and the recovery path is typing a saved code after losing the authenticator. Lowercase and strip non-hex characters before comparing in both handlers.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same case-sensitive indexOf comparison that rejects backup codes containing uppercase hex characters. Its additional concerns about separators do not change the underlying match.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write

After a backup code matches, the handler nulls that array slot and writes the re-encrypted list with a plain read-modify-write. The user row is not locked and the write is not conditional on the ciphertext that was just read. Two overlapping logins with the same code both see it as unused and both get a session, so the code is not single-use. Two overlapping logins with different codes can also lose an update: each write is based on a stale list, and the last write puts the other code back. Consume the code in a transaction that locks the user row, or compare-and-swap on the previous ciphertext, and only then issue the session.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same non-atomic backup-code read-modify-write race: concurrent logins can read the same unused code and both successfully consume it, violating one-time-use semantics. The candidate adds a related lost-update scenario and mitigation suggestions without changing the underlying issue.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup code alone can log in if any TOTP value is also sent

The new backup-code branch in credentials authorize never checks the primary factor. Password verification only runs when credentials.totpCode is empty, and non-CAL users are rejected only when totpCode is empty. A caller who knows the email and one backup code can sign in by posting any non-empty totpCode (for example "000000") with that backup code and a wrong or empty password. The password check and the identity-provider check are both skipped, and a matching backup code creates a session. A backup code then replaces the password or the IdP login, not only the authenticator, which contradicts the UI copy. The disable endpoint does not have this hole: it verifies the CAL password before accepting a backup code. This branch must verify the primary factor even when totpCode is present, and a non-CAL account must not be able to finish credentials login with only a backup code.

Dismissing the backup-code step skips onEnable and loses the codes

A successful TOTP enable used to call onEnable() immediately. It now only moves to the backup-code step, and onEnable() runs only from the Close button. The dialog still takes onOpenChange, so Escape, the overlay, or the X control closes it without onEnable() or resetState(). Two-factor is already enabled on the server, but the parent is not notified, so the settings switch stays off and a later toggle tries to enable again and fails as already enabled. The codes live only in this component's state, are never shown again, and there is no regenerate action, so that dismiss also permanently drops the only copy. A refresh on this step has the same result. Block dismissal until the user finishes, or treat every close of this step as completion and call onEnable().

Download control nests a button in an anchor inside the enable form

The download control is a Button wrapped in an anchor with the blob URL, inside the form whose submit handler is handleEnable. Interactive content inside an anchor is invalid HTML, and browsers often do not follow the link when the click target is a button, so Download can save nothing. The button also does not set type="button". The copy and close buttons in this footer call preventDefault because a click submits the form; this control cannot do that without also cancelling the download. A click can therefore POST /api/auth/two-factor/totp/enable again after 2FA is already on, while the file may not download. Use a type="button" control that starts the blob download without wrapping a button in an anchor.

Lost-access button also submits the disable form

The new Lost access / Go back button is inside the disable Form and neither sets type="button" nor calls preventDefault. The real disable control in the same footer is type="submit", and the enable modal's non-submit actions call preventDefault because clicks in these forms submit. Clicking Lost access therefore also runs handleDisable. The click handler clears the code fields first, so the request is sent with an empty TOTP and backup code, the API returns a second-factor or incorrect-code error, and that error is shown just for switching modes. This disable path is untested. Set type="button" on the toggle.

Backup-code auth is untested and the enable assertion cannot fail

The enable-and-login test never closes the new backup-code step, so onEnable() does not run and the switch is not updated. It then asserts expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy(). isChecked() returns a Promise, and a Promise object is always truthy, so the assertion passes without 2FA being enabled. The test can also log out before the enable request finishes. The new steps only check that a download is named cal-backup-codes.txt and that a success toast appears; they do not read the file or use a code. Nothing covers login with a backup code, single-use consumption, a password-less backup-code attempt, or disabling 2FA with a backup code. Those are the paths with the auth and race bugs.

Copy toast fires before the clipboard write succeeds

The copy handler calls navigator.clipboard.writeText without awaiting or catching it, then immediately shows a success toast. writeText rejects when permission is denied or the clipboard API is missing. The user is told the codes were copied, closes the dialog, and cannot view them again. Await the write and toast only on success; show an error if it fails.

Empty backup-code submit shows no error

The login form sets noValidate, and the zod schema only validates email and password before passthrough, so the BackupCode required and minLength attributes are not enforced. Submitting Lost access with an empty code sends a falsy backupCode. The server treats that as not using a backup code, requires a TOTP code, and returns SecondFactorRequired. This handler only sets twoFactorRequired and does not set an error, so the submit looks like it did nothing. Validate backupCode on that step and show an error for an empty submission.

Missing-backup-codes text points at a settings action that does not exist

missing_backup_codes says to generate codes in settings. Users who enabled 2FA before this column existed, and anyone with null backupCodes, see this on login and when disabling 2FA. There is no settings action to generate codes while 2FA is already on: setup returns two-factor-already-enabled, and codes are only created during enable. The instruction cannot be followed. Tell them to disable and re-enable 2FA with the authenticator, or add a real regenerate action and then point at it.

Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

The candidate clarifies that the lookup executes when externalCalendarId is missing and explains the resulting failures.

This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

false_positives.candidate:
Google Meet booking throws when destinationCalendar is missing

EventManager.create now takes the first destinationCalendar and reads .integration with no null check. If the list is null, undefined, or [] (the value many callers now pass when nobody has a destination calendar), destructuring yields undefined and this throws TypeError before any video or calendar work. Previously optional chaining treated a missing calendar as not Google and replaced Meet with integrations:daily. Any Google Meet booking without a destination calendar, including confirmation and payment flows that pass [], now fails the whole create instead of falling back to Cal Video.

Video references no longer store credentialId

referencesToCreate used to persist result.credentialId for non-calendar results and now stores undefined whenever the result is not a calendar type. updateLocation in this same file still copies result.credentialId, so this is an accidental drop. handleCancelBooking only calls deleteMeeting when the video BookingReference has a credentialId, and there is no fallback lookup by integration type. New bookings will therefore not record the video credential, and cancelling them leaves the Zoom, Daily, or other video room in place.

Collective host calendars are dropped from the event

Other hosts' destination calendars are only appended with optional chaining. If neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, the field is null and the push is a no-op, so every other host is discarded. createAllCalendarEvents then falls back to credentials whose type is exactly "calendar", which never matches google_calendar, office365_calendar, and the rest, so nobody gets a calendar event. Separately, when the event type does have a destination calendar, that single calendar replaces the organizer's personal calendar, and only users.slice(1) are added, so the organizer's own calendar is never included. The stated goal that every collective host with a calendar app receives an event is not met in either case.

Only the first destination calendar is stored on the booking

Booking.destinationCalendar is a single relation and the create payload connects only evt.destinationCalendar[0]. The other hosts' calendars exist only on the in-memory event used for the immediate create. Stripe payment_intent.succeeded and setup_intent.succeeded, and PayPal handlePaymentSuccess, rebuild CalendarEvent from that one booking or user record and call EventManager.create. confirm.handler does the same and passes the evt to handleConfirmation. Collective bookings whose calendar events are created after payment or after organizer approval therefore only write the first calendar; every other host is skipped even if the initial assembly was correct.

Cancelling a recurring series leaves other hosts' events

The non-recurring branch deletes each calendar reference with that reference's credential. The all-remaining recurring branch was not updated: it still loads only the booking owner's calendar credentials and, for each instance, uses find() so only the first _calendar reference is deleted. It is also nested inside the new per-reference loop, so that incomplete deletion runs once per calendar reference. Other hosts' credentials are never loaded, Google 404s from the wrong token are treated as success, and the booking is already marked cancelled. After "cancel all remaining", secondary hosts keep the series on their calendars and stay busy.

Google create falls back to primary instead of the chosen calendar

createEvent selects the calendar only by matching destinationCalendar.credentialId to the credential used for the call. EventManager still has a legacy path for destination calendars with no credentialId, and that path calls createEvent without an external id. The find then misses, and the insert uses "primary" instead of the destination calendar's externalId, so the event is written to the wrong calendar and reported as success. The follow-up hangout-link patch at line 168 passes selectedCalendar with no primary fallback, so that patch runs with an undefined calendarId and the Meet link is never written into the description. The stored booking reference external id will not match the calendar that was actually written.

Location updates store calendar references without ids

updateLocation now sets externalCalendarId and credentialId from the EventResult. CalendarManager.updateEvent does not return either field (it also does not return externalId), and calendar updates populate updatedEvent rather than createdEvent. New booking references created by edit location therefore have an empty uid and no calendar credential or external calendar id. Previously those ids were copied from the destination calendar. The new multi-reference cancel path treats a missing credentialId as a legacy reference and calls deleteEvent on every calendar credential with a null external id, which no longer falls back to the real destination calendar.

Seat-merge reschedule deletes only the first old calendar event

updateAllCalendarEvents was changed to update every calendar reference, but the newBookingId merge path still does references.find() and deletes only the first _calendar reference. When a seated booking is moved onto an existing slot, every other host's old calendar event is left in place at the original time. Those hosts remain busy for a booking that has already been merged away.

Webhook destinationCalendar shape is a breaking, inconsistent change

destinationCalendar on CalendarEvent changed from a single object or null to an array or null, and that object is sent on booking webhooks. Consumers that read payload.destinationCalendar.externalId or .integration will now see an array (or crash). The PR is marked non-breaking, but this is a public payload change. Callers are also inconsistent: handleNewBooking sends null when there is no calendar, while confirm, payment webhooks, and cancel send []. The e2e suite only updated BOOKING_REJECTED to expect []; BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED still expect null, so the contract is not locked down.

No test covers multi-host calendar create or cleanup

The only test change is a webhook fixture expecting destinationCalendar: [] for BOOKING_REJECTED. Nothing books a collective event with two hosts on different calendar providers and asserts one successful write per host credential, and nothing asserts that cancel, reschedule, and payment-confirmation paths create or delete every stored booking reference. The checklist explicitly says no tests were added. The provider, recurring-cancel, and deferred-create bugs above would not be caught by CI.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
WipeMyCal reschedule drops calendar and video cleanup

The WipeMyCal reschedule handler awaits getCalendar inside bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...). forEach does not await async callbacks and ignores what they return, so the surrounding try/catch never handles rejections. Because app modules are now dynamic imports, getCalendar yields before calendar.deleteEvent runs, and the video branch returns deleteMeeting without awaiting it even though deleteMeeting now waits on getVideoAdapters before deleting the meeting. The handler proceeds to send the reschedule email and returns true while that work is still suspended. Before this change getCalendar was sync, so the calendar delete was started before the function moved on. On serverless the process can exit when the handler returns, leaving the old calendar event and video room in place after the booking is marked cancelled. Use for...of or Promise.all and await both provider deletes before sending email.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same async-forEach bug: callbacks are not awaited, so cleanup runs fire-and-forget, rejections escape the surrounding try/catch, and the handler may return before deletions finish. It also recommends the same fixes, for...of or Promise.all with awaited operations.

false_positives.candidate:
requestReschedule does not wait for provider cancellation

requestReschedule awaits getCalendar inside bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...). forEach does not join those promises, so the mutation continues, sends the reschedule email and BOOKING_CANCELLED webhooks, and resolves while calendar deletion is still suspended on the app-store dynamic import. The video branch only returns deleteMeeting from that callback; deleteMeeting now awaits getVideoAdapters before it calls the provider, so that cleanup is deferred the same way and is also not awaited. The booking row is already set to CANCELLED before this loop. If the worker stops when the tRPC mutation returns, which is typical on serverless, the provider calls never run and the old calendar event and video room remain. There is no try/catch around the loop, so a rejection is unhandled rather than a failed mutation. Await the references with for...of or Promise.all, including deleteEvent and deleteMeeting, before email or webhooks.

Recurring cancel never joins calendar deletions

Cancelling all remaining instances of a recurring booking deletes external calendar events with credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(await calendar.deleteEvent(...)) }). forEach does not return those promises, and the push onto apiDeletes happens only after deleteEvent has already resolved, so the later await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) neither starts nor waits for this work. This change made getCalendar async (it now awaits a dynamic import) while leaving this loop in place; the non-recurring branch just below was correctly rewritten as a for...of that awaits getCalendar and pushes the in-flight deleteEvent promise. Previously getCalendar was synchronous, so deleteEvent was invoked before the callback's first await and the provider request was at least started. Now the callback suspends before deleteEvent is issued. The handler can mark the series CANCELLED, send the cancellation email, and return while those events are still on the external calendar; on serverless the continuations are often dropped. Failures are unhandled rejections. Replace the forEach with a for...of or Promise.all and include each deleteEvent promise in apiDeletes before awaiting them.

Drift wait in test_basic is a no-op, so the flush assertion is racy

test_basic monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op, then after setting current_drift to 9000 calls time.sleep(0.1) with a comment that it gives the flusher time to run. That sleep is the patched no-op, so it does not wait. step.join() then sets the shared stopped flag immediately, and the flusher only produces inside `while not stopped`. If the flusher thread does not get the GIL between the drift write and that flag, it exits without flushing and `(msg,) = messages` fails. The same patch turns SpanFlusher.join's time.sleep(0.1) into a GIL-holding busy spin, so whether the test passes depends on accidental thread switches. The sleep added in this PR does not close the race it was meant to fix.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Replacing a flusher does not wait for the old one to stop

When a flusher is dead or hung, _ensure_processes_alive kill()s it and immediately calls _create_process_for_shards for the same shards, without join()ing the old process. kill()/os.kill returns when the signal is queued, not when the process has exited; a process blocked in a syscall keeps running until the call returns, and SIGKILL does not cancel an in-flight Redis flush or Kafka produce. The old Process is then overwritten in self.processes, so nothing ever waits for it. The replacement starts flush_segments on the same shards while the old process may already have produced those segments and not yet called done_flush_segments, so the same segment is written to buffered-segments twice (or a partial delete races the new read). The kill is also skipped for threading.Thread (the produce_to_pipe path) because it is guarded by isinstance(..., multiprocessing.Process), and that check does not match the spawn-context process type this file annotates as multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess if that class is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process — in that case a hung production flusher is never killed and a second flusher is started beside it. A slow produce that exceeds spans.buffer.flusher.max-unhealthy-seconds takes this path, not only hard crashes.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate's main point is that the old process is never joined. It also explicitly says the isinstance(..., multiprocessing.Process) check may not match SpawnProcess, so a hung flusher would never be killed. That is the same issue as the golden comment, though the candidate hedges it with 'if'.
