.small-action is now a flex row (flexbox() and align-items(center) at the top of the rule), but its delete/recover button is still only positioned with float: right. Float does not apply to flex items, so a direct-child button (the usual Discourse small-action markup: avatar, description, then the times button) stays in source order instead of pinning to the row's right edge. Even if the button is nested in .small-action-desc, that description is a default flex item (flex: 0 1 auto, no flex-grow) and now has only padding: 0 1.5% instead of a full-width block with 4em left padding, so a float inside it aligns to the text, not the far side of the post. The X that used to sit at the right of closed/pinned/similar action rows now sits immediately beside the action text and is easy to mis-click next to the username. Browsers that ignore flexbox still honor .topic-avatar { float: left }, and the 4em padding that kept the description clear of that 45px icon is gone, so the text runs through the icon. Give the description flex: 1 and min-width: 0, put margin-left: auto and flex-shrink: 0 on the button, and stop using float for either child.

false_negatives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
website_name bypasses anonymous TL0 website hiding

website_name is computed from the profile website, but it is not subject to the same anonymous trust-level-0 restriction as website. untrusted_attributes only defines include_<attr>? for bio, location, website, and the background fields, and that guard is what stops anonymous viewers (and crawlers hitting /users/:username.json) from seeing a new user's website. The new include_website_name method is never called: this serializer, like ActiveModel Serializers 0.8, only invokes include_website_name? (question mark), which is how every other include hook in this file is named. Even if it were renamed, it only returns website.present? and never calls scope.restrict_user_fields?(object). Previously the client derived the label from model.website, so when website was omitted the globe link disappeared. Now an anonymous profile request for a TL0 user omits website but still receives website_name (host, and host+path when the comparison matches), and the template renders it. That restores the spam-visible website the restriction exists to hide. Put :website_name in untrusted_attributes and delete this include method; a later include_website_name? that only checks website.present? would override the macro and keep the leak. As written, users with a blank website also always get "website_name": null, because the include hook does not run.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate says the include_website_name method lacks the ? suffix, so the hook is never called. That is the golden comment's core issue. The candidate's main focus is a different concern (bypassing the TL0 restriction), but it explicitly identifies the missing ? and its consequence. It does not mention the string mutation point.

false_positives.candidate:
Same-domain check mis-classifies hosts

website_name's host comparison does not match "same domain", so the path is added for unrelated sites and omitted for equivalent ones. Equality and ends_with? are case-sensitive, but Ruby's URI parser keeps host case and Discourse.current_hostname is lowercase: http://Example.com/user on a forum at example.com fails every branch and displays Example.com with no path. The sibling branch (same label count > 2, then compare everything after the first label) treats evil.co.uk and forum.co.uk, or a.github.io and b.github.io, as the same site because the shared suffix is a public suffix, and appends the path. The else branch's discourse_host.ends_with?("." + website_host) is true for any suffix, so a website host of com matches every *.com forum and the label becomes com plus the path. The parent check is one-way: example.com on a www.example.com forum includes the path, but http://www.example.com/user on an example.com forum does not, because the label counts differ and example.com does not end with .www.example.com. Profile labels will therefore show paths for unrelated domains and hide paths for the same site entered with different case or a www prefix.

Displayed website name drops non-default ports

website_name keeps only URI#host, which never includes the port, then optionally appends the path. The removed client label used website.split("/")[2], so http://example.com:8443/app was shown as example.com:8443. It is now shown as example.com when the host is unrelated, or example.com/app when the host comparison matches. The href is still the original URL, but the visible text identifies the default port. Any profile website on a non-default port is mislabeled, including links that are not on the forum domain.

Specs miss the TL0 leak and domain edge cases

The anonymous TL0 example still only asserts that bio, location, website, and background keys are absent, and it never sets a website. website_name is therefore free to appear in that JSON (as a host/path, or as null when the include hook does not run) without failing the suite. The new examples only stub current_hostname to discourse.org, example.com, and forums.example.com against an already-lowercased http://example.com/user, so they do not catch case-sensitive misses, port stripping, the www child case, or false matches such as another *.co.uk host or a website host of com. Those are the paths that produce the wrong label or the privacy leak, and the added specs still pass if they ship.

true_positives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feed URL is passed to Kernel#open with no scheme check

poll_feed passes SiteSetting.feed_polling_url directly to open() after requiring open-uri. Nothing checks that the setting is an http or https URL. In Ruby, open('|...') spawns a shell and open('/path') reads a local file; open-uri only special-cases strings that look like URLs. A feed setting of a pipe command or filesystem path (admin UI, API, or script running as an admin) becomes command execution or local file read on the next poll. http URLs are also fetched with no timeout, redirect allowlist, or response size limit, so a slow or huge feed blocks a worker and can exhaust memory.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to the same code: open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) runs without any URL validation. The golden comment frames the impact as SSRF, letting the server fetch arbitrary URLs. The candidate frames it as command execution and local file read via Kernel#open. Both identify the same unvalidated-open issue on the same line, and the candidate also mentions unrestricted http fetching.

true_positives.golden_comment: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Resize postMessage uses the full referer as targetOrigin

The embed layout calls parent.postMessage(message, request.referer). The second argument must be an origin (scheme://host[:port]), but request.referer is a full URL with path and query. Browsers then throw or drop the message (target origin does not match the parent). ERB escaping also turns `&` in the referer into `&`, so the string would not match even without a path. embed.js only grows the iframe from that discourse-resize message and sets scrolling=no, so comments stay clipped at the default iframe height.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate makes the same point as the golden comment. postMessage is given the full referer URL as targetOrigin instead of the origin, so the message is dropped and the iframe never resizes. Its extra details about ERB escaping and clipped height are additions, not a different issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Imported HTML is stored and rendered without sanitization

Post#cook returns the raw body unchanged when cook_method is raw_html, and TopicEmbed.import saves remote HTML with that cook method (skip_validations: true). PollFeed (poll_feed.rb:35) runs CGI.unescapeHTML on the feed body first, which turns escaped tags back into real markup, and never runs Sanitize. import_remote only whitelists a few tags/attributes and still allows javascript: href/src values. TopicEmbed.import also interpolates the source URL, unescaped, into an href (topic_embed.rb:13). Cooked HTML is treated as trusted in the forum UI, and best.html.erb:19 emits it with `raw`. A feed item or imported page can therefore store script or javascript: links that execute in the Discourse origin for every viewer of the topic or embed.
true_positives.reasoning: The golden comment names two problems: a NoMethodError when contents is nil, and XSS from the url being interpolated into the HTML without escaping. The candidate explicitly states that TopicEmbed.import interpolates the source URL unescaped into an href (topic_embed.rb:13) and frames it as an XSS risk, so it covers the XSS half. It misses the nil case, but the XSS issue is a substantive match.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Embed template has a Ruby syntax error and cannot render

best.html.erb closes its first conditional with `<%- end if %>` (line 6). That compiles to `end if`, which is a Ruby syntax error, so ActionView raises when an existing embed topic is rendered and the iframe gets a 500. The new controller spec never renders views, so it still passes. On-demand and feed-imported embeds cannot display comments until this is a plain `end`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same problem: the ERB block is closed with `end if`, which is a Ruby syntax error and fails at render time. Both say the fix is a plain `end`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feed poll crashes on typical RSS items

poll_feed always calls i.content.scrub and CGI.unescapeHTML. SimpleRSS exposes standard RSS 2.0 bodies as description (and content:encoded as content_encoded), not content, so i.content is missing or nil and this raises NoMethodError. String#scrub itself only exists on Ruby 2.1+, so the same line crashes on Ruby 1.9/2.0 even when content is present. There is no per-item rescue, and the job sets retry: false, so one bad item aborts the rest of that hourly import. Titles and links are also used unchecked, so a blank title fails the same way.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to the same bug: poll_feed calls i.content.scrub, but RSS feeds usually supply description rather than content, so content is nil and the call raises NoMethodError. The candidate's extra points (Ruby version, retry: false) don't change that the core issue matches.

false_positives.candidate:
Public embed endpoint triggers unbounded server-side fetches

EmbedController#best is an unauthenticated GET. Its only gate is that the Referer host equals embeddable_host (embed_controller.rb:26), which any non-browser client can spoof. It then enqueues RetrieveTopic for the caller-supplied embed_url (embed_controller.rb:15). TopicRetriever only compares URI#host to that setting and does not restrict scheme or port (topic_retriever.rb:15). import_remote then calls open(url).read with no timeout or size cap. open-uri follows redirects, so a path on the configured host that 302s to a link-local or internal URL is fetched from the Discourse server, and the body is loaded entirely into memory. Distinct embed_urls each enqueue work, so this is also a job-queue and memory DoS, and a successful HTML response is imported as a topic posted by embed_by_username.

Loading embed never reliably advances to the topic

When no TopicEmbed exists, EmbedController renders loading and then calls discourse_expires_in 1.minute (embed_controller.rb:19), marking that response cacheable. The loading page reloads itself after 30 seconds via location.reload() with no cache-busting flag, so the browser may reuse the fresh cached loading document and never notice that the topic was created. If the reload does hit the server, authorization still requires the Referer host to be embeddable_host. A reload's Referer is often the iframe's own Discourse URL or empty, not the original parent page, so ensure_embeddable returns InvalidAccess and the iframe stays on the error or loading state.

Host-spam check still blocks imports for a new embed user

TopicEmbed.import creates the topic with skip_validations: true, but PostCreator still runs rollback_if_host_spam_detected before save. has_host_spam? is skipped only for trust level basic and above, and newuser_spam_host_threshold defaults to 3. A newly created embed_by_username account is trust level 0, and imported HTML usually contains several links to the same host, so the create transaction is rolled back. import still treats the returned post object as present and TopicEmbed.create! then fails on a null post_id. Feed polling and on-demand retrieve both fail for ordinary articles unless the configured user is already TL1+.

embed_url is limited to 255 characters

embed_url is a Rails string column, created as varchar(255), with a unique index on that column. Article and tracking URLs often exceed 255 characters. PostgreSQL then raises a string-truncation error, the import transaction rolls back, and that page can never be embedded. There is no foreign key or dependent: :destroy on topic_id/post_id either, so deleting the topic leaves a topic_embeds row; topic_id_for_embed still returns the dead id, TopicView errors, and TopicRetriever skips the URL because the row exists, so the embed never heals.

Protocol-relative URLs are rewritten onto the article host

absolutize_urls treats every href and src that starts with `/` as a root-relative path and strips leading slashes before prefixing the article origin. Protocol-relative URLs such as //cdn.example.com/img.png start with `/`, so they become http://article-host/cdn.example.com/img.png. Relative links that do not start with `/` (img.png, ../img.png) are left untouched. Imported RSS and readability HTML commonly uses both forms, so images and links in the created topic are broken. The port logic also drops the port whenever it is 80 or 443, so https on port 80 or http on port 443 is rewritten to the wrong default port.

Retrieve throttle can lock a URL forever

retrieved_recently? claims the per-URL lock with SETNX and only then sets a 60 second TTL in a second command. If the process dies between those calls, retrieved:<url> is left with no expiry. Later retrieves treat the URL as recently fetched forever, unless the viewer is staff (no_throttle). The key is also set before a successful fetch, so a crash or a failed fetch in that window permanently prevents import of that embed URL. SET with NX and EX in one command would avoid the stuck key.

Every embed miss synchronously imports the entire feed

On a cache miss, perform_retrieve calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute inline before fetching the requested URL. That downloads the whole feed and runs TopicEmbed.import for every item, inside the RetrieveTopic worker that was enqueued just to import one page. One iframe view can occupy a Sidekiq thread for the full feed and create or revise every feed topic. The redis lock only lasts 60 seconds, so a slow poll overlaps the next retrieve and starts another full import. The scheduled job already polls hourly; this path should not repeat that work synchronously.

Disqus import now requires live fetches and drops category and dates

The importer used to create a local permalink topic with the XML thread's created_at and an optional --category. It now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote for t[:link] and the category option was removed, so every thread is fetched over HTTP, posted as the current time, and lands in the default category. import_remote is not rescued: one missing link, non-http link, timeout, or readability failure raises and aborts the rest of the export. The task can no longer import from the XML file alone.

Embeddable host comparison is case-sensitive

invalid_host? and EmbedController#ensure_embeddable compare SiteSetting.embeddable_host to URI#host with != and do not downcase either side. Hostnames are case-insensitive, but Ruby's URI#host keeps the original case, so a referer or embed_url of http://EvilTrout.com is rejected when the setting is eviltrout.com. The embed then 403s or never imports even though the host is the configured one.

Poll feed specs do not exercise the guards they name

The examples that claim execute requires feed_polling_url and embed_by_username never stub feed_polling_enabled? to true. That setting defaults to false, so execute returns before those checks and the examples pass even if the url or username guard is deleted. Nothing calls poll_feed, so nil content, non-http item links, Kernel#open behavior, and TopicEmbed.import failures are untested. The embed controller spec also does not render views, which is why the best.html.erb syntax error is invisible to CI.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Second downsize definition discards the width/height API

Ruby has no overloading, so the second OptimizedImage.downsize at app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 replaces the width/height method just above it at line 145 (Ruby warns "method redefined; discarding old downsize"). The wrapper that would build a "#{max_width}x#{max_height}" geometry is therefore dead, and the previous public signature downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) no longer exists. This pull request does not update any other call sites. A caller that still passes an options hash as a fifth argument raises ArgumentError (5 for 4). A four-argument call such as downsize(from, to, 400, 300) binds 400 as the geometry string and 300 as opts, so ImageMagick shrinks to width 400 instead of 400x300, and opts[:allow_animation] raises TypeError because opts is an Integer. optimize was also changed from separate width and height arguments to a single dimensions string, so direct callers of optimize break the same way. Keep one method that accepts either a geometry string or numeric width and height, and update every caller.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same problem. downsize is defined twice, the second definition (taking a dimensions string) overrides the first (taking width/height), and callers that pass separate arguments break.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Hardcoded 10MB cap ignores image and attachment settings

validateUploadedFile used to limit uploads with Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] (max_image_size_kb for images, max_attachment_size_kb for everything else). Line 182 now hardcodes 10 * 1024 KB for both types. Attachments are not downsized, and UploadsController never reads max_attachment_size_kb, so the browser will accept attachments the admin setting forbids (they fail late, or are stored if nothing else checks) and will reject attachments larger than 10MB even when that setting allows them. Images are capped at 10MB even when max_image_size_kb is higher, so previously valid uploads never reach the server downsize path. If max_image_size_kb is already at least 10240, a browser upload can never exceed the server downsize threshold and this feature does not run for normal uploads. The same magic number is repeated in the HTTP 413 alert (utilities.js:246), which tells the user the limit is 10240 KB regardless of the web server or site setting, and in API URL fetches (uploads_controller.rb:55, FileHelper.download(..., 10.megabytes)), which used to stop at SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes and now always pulls up to 10MB, including non-images. The client cap, the 413 text, and the download ceiling need to come from site settings: a real pre-downsize image ceiling, and max_attachment_size_kb for other files.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate flags the same problem as the golden comment. The hardcoded 10*1024 KB limit replaces the per-type Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] check, so the client limit diverges from server settings. It also notes the same hardcoded value in the 413 handler.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
In-place downsize runs on an extensionless tempfile

create_upload downsizes with OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails) at uploads_controller.rb:67. Input and output are the same path. ImageMagick does not support that: convert can truncate the destination before it finishes reading, leaving a zero-byte or corrupt image, and the original bytes are already overwritten so there is no fallback. The false return value is ignored, so Upload.create_for on line 72 stores the damaged file. The path is also the wrong file identity. Rack multipart tempfiles are named like /tmp/RackMultipart... with no suffix, and the URL download uses the prefix discourse-upload-#{type} rather than the real extension; the original name lives only in filename. ImageMagick picks the output coder from the destination suffix, so the write can fail with no encode delegate or emit bytes that do not match filename and content_type. Animation is dropped for the same reason: OptimizedImage.optimize (optimized_image.rb:155) adds the gifsicle path only when the path matches /\.GIF$/i. An extensionless tempfile never matches, so every oversized GIF goes through convert ...[0], which keeps only the first frame. allow_animated_thumbnails therefore cannot preserve animation. Even if the path ended in .gif, gifsicle --resize-fit (optimized_image.rb:120) expects pixel geometry such as 100x100, not ImageMagick's 80%, so that branch would fail too. Tempfile#size is an fstat of the still-open descriptor; if convert replaces the path by rename, the size loop and the filesize passed to create_for keep seeing the old inode. Downsize into a new tempfile that keeps the original extension, and only replace the upload if the command succeeds and the new file is non-empty.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly says gifsicle --resize-fit expects pixel geometry such as 100x100, not '80%', so the animated branch would fail. That is the golden issue. It sits among other concerns, but it is clearly stated.

true_positives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Downsize loop can finish still over the limit

The loop at uploads_controller.rb:66 calls OptimizedImage.downsize up to five times and ignores a false return. convert_with returns false when ImageMagick or gifsicle exits non-zero or ImageOptim raises, and it throws away stderr (&> /dev/null), so a failed pass leaves the file unchanged or truncated while the loop only decrements attempt. It then always calls Upload.create_for with no check that the file is under SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. Each pass is a relative 80% geometry shrink plus another lossy re-encode and ImageOptim run, not a resize aimed at the byte limit. Five passes leave about 33% of the linear dimensions (about 10% of the pixels), which is not enough when the upload is near the new 10MB client ceiling and max_image_size_kb is much smaller. The while condition uses tempfile.size, which will not change if the tool replaced the path and the open descriptor still stats the old inode, so all five attempts run anyway. Multipart uploads also have no upper bound before convert, unlike the 10MB URL download, so any logged-in user who can post a large body can force five ImageMagick plus ImageOptim runs on an arbitrarily large image (and on a small decompression bomb just over the setting) on the synchronous request thread or on Scheduler::Defer. Stop when downsize fails, return an error if the file is still over the limit, and refuse files above a hard maximum before invoking convert.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate says the while condition uses tempfile.size, which won't change if the file was replaced while the descriptor still stats the old inode. That is the stale cached size problem the golden comment describes, and it leads to incorrect loop behavior. The candidate also raises other concerns, but this specific point matches.

false_positives.candidate:
No tests for downsizing or the new size caps

The new downsize loop in UploadsController#create_upload and the client/API limit changes ship with no tests. Nothing covers an image over max_image_size_kb being stored under that limit, convert failing or still being over the limit after five passes, an animated GIF keeping or losing frames, attachments still honoring max_attachment_size_kb, or OptimizedImage.downsize accepting both a geometry string and numeric width/height. Those are the paths this change gets wrong, and they will not be caught before merge.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Missing TopicUser 500s, and save! does not record an explicit choice

unsubscribe does TopicUser.find_by and immediately reads tu.notification_level. If the logged-in viewer has no topic_users row (the URL is not bound to the email recipient; any logged-in user who can see the topic can open it), tu is nil and this raises NoMethodError. tu.save! also bypasses TopicUser.change, which is what sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed, sets notifications_changed_at, creates a missing row, and publishes /topic/:id on MessageBus. The mailer creates the recipient row with TopicUser.change(last_emailed_post_number:) and does not set a reason, so reason often stays nil. update_last_read then auto-upgrades notification_level back to tracking when notifications_reason_id is null and view time exceeds the auto-track threshold, and TopicUser.auto_track does the same when reason is nil. The unsubscribe can be silently undone on a later visit, and other open tabs are not notified. Use TopicUser.change so a missing row is created and the user's choice is sticky.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly says tu can be nil when no TopicUser row exists, which raises NoMethodError when tu.notification_level is read. That is the same nil pointer issue as the golden comment. The candidate also raises extra points, but these do not change the match.

false_positives.candidate:
render :show runs before canonical_url is set

perform_show_response now calls render :show inside the HTML branch (topics_controller.rb:500). TopicsController#show only calls canonical_url after perform_show_response returns (line 87). Previously the HTML branch did not render, so Rails implicit render ran after the action finished and the layout still saw @canonical_url. render evaluates the show template and layout immediately, so @canonical_url is still nil and every topic HTML response loses its canonical link. This is a silent site-wide regression, not limited to unsubscribe. Move the render back out of the shared method, or set the canonical URL before rendering.

Unsubscribe mutates notification state on a cookie-authenticated GET

config/routes.rb registers topics#unsubscribe as GET (t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and t/:topic_id/unsubscribe), and the action writes TopicUser.notification_level at topics_controller.rb:107-113 with no per-user token. Topic#unsubscribe_url (topic.rb:719) is only /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe, the same for every recipient, unlike the existing digest link email/unsubscribe/:key. Rails forgery protection does not cover GET, so any page can include that URL as an image or link and, for a logged-in victim, downgrade or mute the topic. Email prefetchers and link scanners that send the user's cookies will do the same without a click. Logged-out recipients are only redirected to login, so the link does not identify or unsubscribe the person who was emailed. The Ember route never calls an unsubscribe API; it only loads the topic. A safe design is a signed, user-specific token, or a GET confirmation page plus a POST that uses TopicUser.change.

Unsubscribe does not stop notifications for watchers and is not idempotent

If notification_level is above regular (tracking=2 or watching=3), unsubscribe sets regular (1); otherwise it sets muted (0). Watching is what causes an email on every new post, and the new copy promises a full stop: server.en.yml unsubscribe_link says "stop receiving notifications about this particular topic", and client.en.yml topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications says "You will stop receiving notifications". After one request those users are still at regular, so replies, mentions, and quotes still notify. The transition is also not idempotent: a second GET (refresh, duplicate fetch, or a scanner request plus the user's click) sees regular and mutes. Outcome depends on how many times the URL is hit, and mute hides the topic from the user's lists, which is stronger than stopping email and is never explained. Always set muted (or another single terminal level) through TopicUser.change, and make repeat requests a no-op.

Unsubscribe template name does not match the route

The route is registered as topicUnsubscribe at /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe (app-route-map.js.es6:13). The new controller, route, and view are all topic-unsubscribe, which Ember resolves as topicUnsubscribe / template topic-unsubscribe. This template lives at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which compiles to the name topic/unsubscribe (nested route topic.unsubscribe). No code renders that name, and there is no templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs. The view also does not set templateName. After the Rails shell loads, the confirmation screen is blank: the stop-notifications copy and topic-notifications-button never appear, so the user cannot see or correct the level the GET just wrote. Move the template to templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs, or nest the route under topic and move the controller and view to match.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime

The same predicate rejects valid slots when a host has two windows on one day (for example 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00): the window that does not contain the slot makes find succeed and the slot is removed, so lunch-break schedules disappear from the booking page for every fixed host, not only round-robin. end is also copied from slotStartTime (line 142) instead of slotEndTime, so a slot that starts inside the window but runs past endTime is still treated as inside. true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly says end is copied from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime, which is the golden issue. It also raises other concerns, but that does not cancel the match.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

A full-day block is stored as an override whose start equals its end, and this callback tries to reject the whole day in that case. The comparison uses === on two dayjs objects, which is reference equality and is never true, so that branch never runs. The following checks only mark a slot outside a window when the slot ends at or before the override start or starts strictly after the override end. A slot that merely overlaps the window — starts before it, ends after it, or straddles a zero-length block — is treated as inside. find() then stops at the first same-day range that does not contain the slot, so two override ranges on one day (a normal custom-hours override with a gap) reject a slot that sits inside the other range and the day shows no bookable override slots. true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly says that comparing two dayjs objects with === checks reference equality and is never true. That is the same bug the golden comment describes. The candidate also raises other issues, but the core issue is present.

false_positives.candidate:
Slots inside a date override skip busy checks and can double-book

checkIfIsAvailable now returns true as soon as a slot falls on a day with a date override and is treated as inside that override, before the busy-interval scan. That scan is the only place calendar conflicts and existing Cal bookings are applied to generated slots, and this function now runs for every fixed host — including ordinary personal and collective events, whose users are marked isFixed. On any day that has a date override, a slot inside the override is therefore shown as free even when the host is already booked, so the same time can be booked twice.

Override date match compares server-local date to UTC date

Whether an override applies to a slot is decided by formatting the offset-adjusted start with a local-mode dayjs and comparing it to slotStartTime.format(), and slotStartTime is in UTC mode (time.utc()). format() on a local-mode instance uses the process timezone, not UTC. Whenever the server timezone is not UTC, the two calendar dates disagree for overrides near midnight and the override is applied to the wrong day or not applied at all, so fixed-host date overrides silently fail outside a UTC process.

Override start/end are converted by adding the invitee-minus-organizer offset and then keeping only hour and minute. That throws away a day boundary. If the shift moves one end across midnight and not the other, endTime is less than startTime; buildSlots discards any range with start >= end. The caller has already deleted that user's normal working hours for the invitee day the raw UTC timestamp fell on, so the day is left with no slots. true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
retryCount is a lost update under overlapping crons

Both failure paths set retryCount to the in-memory reminder.retryCount + 1 instead of an atomic increment, and the same pattern is in the catch. This route has no lock and does a Twilio request per reminder, so a second invocation can overlap a slow run. Both read the same count, both call scheduleSMS, and both write the same next value, so the stop-after-two-failures cap is not enforced and the attendee can get duplicate texts. A failure write can also raise retryCount above 1 on a row the other run already marked scheduled, which the new deleteMany then removes along with its SID. Use an atomic increment and a conditional update that only matches scheduled false (and the id).
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate describes the same bug: retryCount is set non-atomically from a stale in-memory value, so concurrent runs can lose updates. It also notes the same pattern in the catch block and recommends an atomic increment, which matches the golden comment.

true_positives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

retryCount cleanup is not limited to unscheduled SMS

The new deleteMany branch matches every WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 and does not filter on method, scheduled, or cancelled. This table also holds EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders, and a scheduled SMS stores the Twilio SID in referenceId so a booking cancellation can stop the message. Failure updates write retryCount from the value read at the start of the run and do not require scheduled = false, so an overlapping run of this cron (no lock, one Twilio call per reminder) can set retryCount to 2 on a row another run already marked scheduled and saved a SID. The next invocation then deletes that row only because retryCount > 1, the SID is gone, and a later cancellation cannot cancel the text. The same predicate will also delete any non-SMS row that exceeds one retry. Restrict this branch to method SMS and scheduled false. The comment above the query still says it only deletes past-due SMS, which is no longer what it does.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly says the retryCount branch has no method filter, that it will delete non-SMS (EMAIL/WHATSAPP) rows, and that it should be restricted to method SMS. This is the same issue as the golden comment.

false_positives.candidate:
Any two errors permanently drop in-window SMS reminders

Every thrown error in the scheduling try, and every falsy scheduleSMS result, increments the same retryCount, and the next cron deletes the row once retryCount > 1. That includes transient failures (Twilio 5xx or rate limits, getBookerBaseUrl, profile lookup), not only permanent ones such as an invalid number. This job loads every unscheduled SMS reminder whose scheduledDate is within 7 days, so two failed ticks during a short outage delete that whole window. Deletion is irreversible and there is no backoff or Twilio error-code check, so those attendees never get the text even after the provider recovers. Missing phone or empty body never hits the retry limit

retryCount is incremented only inside the branch that actually calls scheduleSMS. If sendTo is missing (SMS_ATTENDEE with a null booking.smsReminderNumber, or SMS_NUMBER with an empty step sendTo) or the rendered body is empty, the handler skips the send and leaves retryCount at 0 and scheduled false, as long as nothing earlier threw. Missing numbers are a common permanent failure and never reach Twilio, so they never reach the new delete. Increment retryCount or delete the row when there is nothing to send.

The new catch updates retryCount and does not handle that update failing. The try also wraps the update that stores the Twilio SID after scheduleSMS returns a message. If that SID update throws, the catch still treats it as a scheduling failure: it increments retryCount and leaves scheduled false and referenceId empty even though Twilio already accepted the message. Later runs schedule more messages for the same reminder, and once retryCount > 1 the row is deleted, so none of those messages can be cancelled. Separately, if the catch update itself throws (Prisma P2025 when a concurrent run already deleted the row), the error escapes the catch, the for-loop stops, and every later reminder in the batch is skipped. Previously this catch only logged. Guard the retry update, and do not count a failure that happens after Twilio has already returned a message as 'not scheduled'.

deleteMany now ORs an unindexed retryCount > 1 predicate with the scheduledDate predicate. WorkflowReminder's index is (method, scheduled, scheduledDate) and was not extended for retryCount in the schema change. An OR against a column with no index typically forces a sequential scan of the whole table on every cron tick, taking row locks for deleted tuples, including email and WhatsApp reminders this job does not own. Split the two cleanups into separate deletes and add an index that matches the retry predicate so this cron does not scan the full reminder table.

This change deletes workflow reminders and adds no tests. Coverage needs to lock the intended contract: scheduleSMS returning null increments retryCount; a thrown error increments it; the row is removed only after retryCount exceeds 1 and only for unscheduled SMS; a successful schedule with a stored referenceId is not deleted; a missing phone or empty body does not remain in the cron until the event time. Team and org authorization SQL is an OR of two branches with no surrounding parenthesis group: ("teamId" = … AND "isTeamBooking" = true) OR ("userId" = ANY(…) AND "isTeamBooking" = false), built at the reduce in buildOrgAuthorizationCondition (line 173) and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition (line 204). The event-type filter is the same shape: ("eventTypeId" = $id) OR ("eventParentId" = $id) at line 106, also returned without an outer group when it is the only filter. getBaseConditions wraps each side only when both auth and filters are present (line 73). With no service filters it returns the bare authorization fragment here. That is the common insights path: this service only filters eventTypeId and memberUserId, and findMany (which AND-merged arbitrary caller where-clauses inside Prisma, so grouping was safe) was removed. Callers must add the time window themselves. WHERE ${getBaseConditions()} AND "startTime" >= $from AND "status" = 'accepted' is parsed as (team branch) OR (personal branch AND startTime >= $from AND status = 'accepted') because AND binds tighter than OR. Every team booking for that team is included regardless of date or status, so team/org insights over-count and ignore caller predicates. A second composition, WHERE ${getAuthorizationConditions()} AND ${getFilterConditions()}, is the obvious translation of the old findMany AND and is also wrong: it parses as (auth AND eventTypeId = $id) OR eventParentId = $id, so any booking whose eventParentId matches is returned even when it fails the org/team/user authorization predicate. That leaks rows for child/managed event types outside the caller's scope. Wrap every returned fragment, including the final OR and this no-filter return, in parentheses (Prisma.sql`(${fragment})`) before it is embedded. The new tests expect the unparenthesized text, so they lock the unsafe shape in.

Team/org SQL is never executed; toEqual does not match nested Prisma.sql

The team-scope assertion here, the org-scope assertion around line 332, and the combined-filter assertion around line 429 compare getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions to a single flat Prisma.sql template via toEqual. Those service methods build the predicate with Array.reduce, so the returned Prisma.Sql values array holds nested Sql fragments; flattening happens only when a query is executed, not in the constructor. vitest deep-equality compares that structure, not rendered SQL, so these three tests fail even when the SQL text matches. NOTHING, user-scope, and single-filter cases are flat templates and can pass, which hides the failure mode. The only query actually sent to the database is the user-scope getBaseConditions case (line 481), which is a pure AND and does not use OR or ANY(array). A passing run therefore does not check team/org authorization, array binding for ANY(${ids}), or the operator-precedence bug when these fragments are AND-ed with a date or status predicate. Execute the team and org fragments with $queryRaw (including an extra AND predicate) and assert both included and excluded rows.

This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

Refresh parser strips real tokens and writes a fake refresh_token

The minimum schema's computed keys are z.string().toString() and z.string().optional().toString(), not wildcards. Those are literal property names (both typically "[object Object]", so the second overwrites the first). They do not match expires_in or expiry_date. When CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, every caller uses this schema, including team credentials that still hit the real provider (the switch does not check whether the sync fetch ran) and Salesforce, which never calls the sync endpoint. safeParse then keeps only access_token and strips refresh_token and expiry. Failures are only logged inside the helper, and cancelled is never set, so the new cron cannot retry. Workflow and step deletion then cascade-delete the WorkflowReminder, which also removes any chance of a later retry; a bulk delete of more than 100 already-scheduled reminders therefore silently leaves the overflow emails queued. It cancels via SendGrid, then neither deletes the WorkflowReminder row nor marks it cancelled, which leaves orphaned or stale records. false_positives.candidate:
Cron deletes due reminders before withdrawing them from SendGrid

scheduleEmailReminders begins by deleteMany-ing every EMAIL WorkflowReminder whose scheduledDate is at or before now, and only afterward loads cancelled=true rows to POST a SendGrid cancel. Any cancelled reminder whose send time has already arrived is removed from the database and never cancelled at SendGrid, so the email is still delivered. With the job running every 15 minutes, a cancellation made after the last tick before scheduledDate (or any run that starts at or after the send time, including a delayed cron) always hits this path. The new cancel query cannot see those rows because they are already gone. SendGrid withdrawal for cancelled=true reminders has to run before this cleanup, and the cleanup must not delete cancelled rows that have not yet been cancelled at SendGrid.

One SendGrid cancel error aborts the batch and drops successful deletes

The new cancel loop awaits every SendGrid POST inside a single try/catch, and only after the whole loop does it await the queued workflowReminder.delete calls. Prisma queries are lazy, so those deletes have not run yet. If any request throws (unknown or already-cancelled batch id, the pending-cancellation cap, a network error), the catch only logs and then the handler goes on to schedule other mail. None of the reminders already cancelled at SendGrid are deleted, and every reminder after the failure is skipped. Those rows stay cancelled=true and are retried on the next run. There is no orderBy and no per-item isolation, so one permanently failing row can be selected first every 15 minutes and block every other cancellation until scheduledDate passes. At that point the opening deleteMany removes the rows without a SendGrid cancel and the emails send. Each reminder needs its own error handling, and a successful cancel must be persisted immediately so it is not retried and cannot poison the queue.

In handleCancelBooking a paid booking is refunded and then returns 'Booking successfully cancelled' before the new reminder-cancellation loop. Before/after-event workflow emails and SMS for paid bookings are therefore neither marked cancelled, deleted, nor withdrawn from SendGrid/Twilio, which is the same production failure this PR is fixing. The cancellation loop has to run on this path as well, and be awaited, before the early return.

The description says the previous SendGrid cancel fix did not work in production, but this change adds no test for the replacement contract. Nothing asserts that booking cancel sets WorkflowReminder.cancelled instead of POSTing scheduled_sends immediately, that reschedule does not use the immediate SendGrid cancel, that the cron withdraws cancelled batches before deleting past-due rows, or that one failed cancel is retried without dropping the rest of the batch. Two overlapping logins with different codes can also lose an update: each write is based on a stale list, and the last write puts the other code back. A backup code then replaces the password or the IdP login, not only the authenticator, which contradicts the UI copy. The disable endpoint does not have this hole: it verifies the CAL password before accepting a backup code. This branch must verify the primary factor even when totpCode is present, and a non-CAL account must not be able to finish credentials login with only a backup code.

The codes live only in this component's state, are never shown again, and there is no regenerate action, so that dismiss also permanently drops the only copy. A refresh on this step has the same result. Block dismissal until the user finishes, or treat every close of this step as completion and call onEnable().

Interactive content inside an anchor is invalid HTML, and browsers often do not follow the link when the click target is a button, so Download can save nothing. The button also does not set type="button". The copy and close buttons in this footer call preventDefault because a click submits the form; this control cannot do that without also cancelling the download. A click can therefore POST /api/auth/two-factor/totp/enable again after 2FA is already on, while the file may not download. The real disable control in the same footer is type="submit", and the enable modal's non-submit actions call preventDefault because clicks in these forms submit. Clicking Lost access therefore also runs handleDisable. The click handler clears the code fields first, so the request is sent with an empty TOTP and backup code, the API returns a second-factor or incorrect-code error, and that error is shown just for switching modes. Backup-code auth is untested and the enable assertion cannot fail

The enable-and-login test never closes the new backup-code step, so onEnable() does not run and the switch is not updated. It then asserts expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy(). isChecked() returns a Promise, and a Promise object is always truthy, so the assertion passes without 2FA being enabled. The test can also log out before the enable request finishes. The new steps only check that a download is named cal-backup-codes.txt and that a success toast appears; they do not read the file or use a code. The copy handler calls navigator.clipboard.writeText without awaiting or catching it, then immediately shows a success toast. writeText rejects when permission is denied or the clipboard API is missing. This handler only sets twoFactorRequired and does not set an error, so the submit looks like it did nothing. Validate backupCode on that step and show an error for an empty submission.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google update/delete fallback can never select a calendar

When externalCalendarId is missing, updateEvent and deleteEvent (same expression at line 317) search destinationCalendar for an entry whose externalId equals that missing value. That comparison is dead: if a calendar id had been passed, the first branch would already have used it. Previously the fallback was destinationCalendar.externalId. updateEvent then calls the Google API with calendarId undefined, so reschedule and location updates fail for any booking reference that has no externalCalendarId. deleteEvent falls through to primary, and a 404 is treated as success (line 335), so cancellation reports success while the event remains on the non-primary calendar.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to the same flawed lookup: searching destinationCalendar for an entry whose externalId equals externalCalendarId, which is self-referential and can never pick a useful calendar. The golden frames it as externalCalendarId being provided and the candidate as it being missing, but the defect in the find expression is the same.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Organization slug condition is inverted

This unrelated change flips slug assignment. Previously slug was set only when team billing was disabled, and requestedSlug only when billing was enabled. requestedSlug is still gated on IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED, but slug is now set in that same case and omitted otherwise. With billing off, new organizations are stored with neither slug nor requestedSlug, so the org subdomain cannot resolve. With billing on, the slug is published immediately and requestedSlug is also set, skipping the hold-for-billing gate.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug: the slug condition was inverted to IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED. As a result, both slug and requestedSlug are set when billing is enabled, and neither is set when it is disabled.

false_positives.candidate:
Google Meet booking throws when destinationCalendar is missing

EventManager.create now takes the first destinationCalendar and reads .integration with no null check. If the list is null, undefined, or [] (the value many callers now pass when nobody has a destination calendar), destructuring yields undefined and this throws TypeError before any video or calendar work. Previously optional chaining treated a missing calendar as not Google and replaced Meet with integrations:daily. Any Google Meet booking without a destination calendar, including confirmation and payment flows that pass [], now fails the whole create instead of falling back to Cal Video.

Video references no longer store credentialId

referencesToCreate used to persist result.credentialId for non-calendar results and now stores undefined whenever the result is not a calendar type. updateLocation in this same file still copies result.credentialId, so this is an accidental drop. handleCancelBooking only calls deleteMeeting when the video BookingReference has a credentialId, and there is no fallback lookup by integration type. New bookings will therefore not record the video credential, and cancelling them leaves the Zoom, Daily, or other video room in place.

Secondary hosts are written to the first destination calendar

createAllCalendarEvents loops each host destination and calls the provider with that host's credential, but it still passes the full destinationCalendar array. Only GoogleCalendarService picks the calendar by credentialId. Office 365 and Lark still use index 0, so a second host's token is aimed at the organizer's calendar id and the API call fails; that host never gets an event. CalDAV/Apple (BaseCalendarService) filters the host's calendars to the organizer's external id, matches nothing, and still returns success, so a booking reference is stored for an event that was never created. Google inserts also set the organizer attendee email from the first destination's externalId, so events written onto another host's calendar are attributed to the main calendar. Office 365 updateEvent and deleteEvent still always call /me/calendar/events/{id} and ignore the target calendar id, so a non-default Office event cannot be rescheduled or removed. Narrow the event to the destination currently being written before calling any provider.

Collective host calendars are dropped from the event

Other hosts' destination calendars are only appended with optional chaining. If neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, the field is null and the push is a no-op, so every other host is discarded. createAllCalendarEvents then falls back to credentials whose type is exactly "calendar", which never matches google_calendar, office365_calendar, and the rest, so nobody gets a calendar event. Separately, when the event type does have a destination calendar, that single calendar replaces the organizer's personal calendar, and only users.slice(1) are added, so the organizer's own calendar is never included. The stated goal that every collective host with a calendar app receives an event is not met in either case.

Only the first destination calendar is stored on the booking

Booking.destinationCalendar is a single relation and the create payload connects only evt.destinationCalendar[0]. The other hosts' calendars exist only on the in-memory event used for the immediate create. Stripe payment_intent.succeeded and setup_intent.succeeded, and PayPal handlePaymentSuccess, rebuild CalendarEvent from that one booking or user record and call EventManager.create. confirm.handler does the same and passes the evt to handleConfirmation. Collective bookings whose calendar events are created after payment or after organizer approval therefore only write the first calendar; every other host is skipped even if the initial assembly was correct.

Cancelling a recurring series leaves other hosts' events

The non-recurring branch deletes each calendar reference with that reference's credential. The all-remaining recurring branch was not updated: it still loads only the booking owner's calendar credentials and, for each instance, uses find() so only the first _calendar reference is deleted. It is also nested inside the new per-reference loop, so that incomplete deletion runs once per calendar reference. Other hosts' credentials are never loaded, Google 404s from the wrong token are treated as success, and the booking is already marked cancelled. After "cancel all remaining", secondary hosts keep the series on their calendars and stay busy.

Google create falls back to primary instead of the chosen calendar

createEvent selects the calendar only by matching destinationCalendar.credentialId to the credential used for the call. EventManager still has a legacy path for destination calendars with no credentialId, and that path calls createEvent without an external id. The find then misses, and the insert uses "primary" instead of the destination calendar's externalId, so the event is written to the wrong calendar and reported as success. The follow-up hangout-link patch at line 168 passes selectedCalendar with no primary fallback, so that patch runs with an undefined calendarId and the Meet link is never written into the description. The stored booking reference external id will not match the calendar that was actually written.

Location updates store calendar references without ids

updateLocation now sets externalCalendarId and credentialId from the EventResult. CalendarManager.updateEvent does not return either field (it also does not return externalId), and calendar updates populate updatedEvent rather than createdEvent. New booking references created by edit location therefore have an empty uid and no calendar credential or external calendar id. Previously those ids were copied from the destination calendar. The new multi-reference cancel path treats a missing credentialId as a legacy reference and calls deleteEvent on every calendar credential with a null external id, which no longer falls back to the real destination calendar.

Seat-merge reschedule deletes only the first old calendar event

updateAllCalendarEvents was changed to update every calendar reference, but the newBookingId merge path still does references.find() and deletes only the first _calendar reference. When a seated booking is moved onto an existing slot, every other host's old calendar event is left in place at the original time. Those hosts remain busy for a booking that has already been merged away.

Webhook destinationCalendar shape is a breaking, inconsistent change

destinationCalendar on CalendarEvent changed from a single object or null to an array or null, and that object is sent on booking webhooks. Consumers that read payload.destinationCalendar.externalId or .integration will now see an array (or crash). The PR is marked non-breaking, but this is a public payload change. Callers are also inconsistent: handleNewBooking sends null when there is no calendar, while confirm, payment webhooks, and cancel send []. The e2e suite only updated BOOKING_REJECTED to expect []; BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED still expect null, so the contract is not locked down.

No test covers multi-host calendar create or cleanup

The only test change is a webhook fixture expecting destinationCalendar: [] for BOOKING_REJECTED. Nothing books a collective event with two hosts on different calendar providers and asserts one successful write per host credential, and nothing asserts that cancel, reschedule, and payment-confirmation paths create or delete every stored booking reference. The checklist explicitly says no tests were added. The provider, recurring-cancel, and deferred-create bugs above would not be caught by CI.

false_negatives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Vital reschedule drops calendar and video cleanup

Reschedule now awaits the async getCalendar inside bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...). Array.forEach never waits for async callbacks and discards their return values, so the try/catch around the loop cannot see failures. getCalendar suspends on a dynamic app import before calendar.deleteEvent is called, and the video branch only returns deleteMeeting, which itself now awaits getVideoAdapters before calling the provider. Nothing awaits those floating promises. The function then sends the reschedule email and returns true. Previously getCalendar was synchronous, so deleteEvent was at least issued before the function continued. After this change a serverless worker can finish the request and freeze before the import resumes, so the cancelled booking's calendar event and video meeting are never removed (the slot stays busy and attendees still see the old event). Rejections become unhandled promise rejections. Await the references with for...of or Promise.all, including both deleteEvent and deleteMeeting, before sending email.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same problem: forEach with async callbacks for calendar and video deletions, where the promises are never awaited. Both note the try/catch cannot catch the failures, that rejections go unhandled, and that cleanup may not complete. Both recommend for...of or Promise.all as the fix.

false_positives.candidate:
WipeMyCal reschedule drops calendar and video cleanup

The WipeMyCal reschedule handler awaits getCalendar inside bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...). forEach does not await async callbacks and ignores what they return, so the surrounding try/catch never handles rejections. Because app modules are now dynamic imports, getCalendar yields before calendar.deleteEvent runs, and the video branch returns deleteMeeting without awaiting it even though deleteMeeting now waits on getVideoAdapters before deleting the meeting. The handler proceeds to send the reschedule email and returns true while that work is still suspended. Before this change getCalendar was sync, so the calendar delete was started before the function moved on. On serverless the process can exit when the handler returns, leaving the old calendar event and video room in place after the booking is marked cancelled. Use for...of or Promise.all and await both provider deletes before sending email.

requestReschedule does not wait for provider cancellation

requestReschedule awaits getCalendar inside bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...). forEach does not join those promises, so the mutation continues, sends the reschedule email and BOOKING_CANCELLED webhooks, and resolves while calendar deletion is still suspended on the app-store dynamic import. The video branch only returns deleteMeeting from that callback; deleteMeeting now awaits getVideoAdapters before it calls the provider, so that cleanup is deferred the same way and is also not awaited. The booking row is already set to CANCELLED before this loop. If the worker stops when the tRPC mutation returns, which is typical on serverless, the provider calls never run and the old calendar event and video room remain. There is no try/catch around the loop, so a rejection is unhandled rather than a failed mutation. Await the references with for...of or Promise.all, including deleteEvent and deleteMeeting, before email or webhooks.

Recurring cancel never joins calendar deletions

Cancelling all remaining instances of a recurring booking deletes external calendar events with credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(await calendar.deleteEvent(...)) }). forEach does not return those promises, and the push onto apiDeletes happens only after deleteEvent has already resolved, so the later await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) neither starts nor waits for this work. This change made getCalendar async (it now awaits a dynamic import) while leaving this loop in place; the non-recurring branch just below was correctly rewritten as a for...of that awaits getCalendar and pushes the in-flight deleteEvent promise. Previously getCalendar was synchronous, so deleteEvent was invoked before the callback's first await and the provider request was at least started. Now the callback suspends before deleteEvent is issued. The handler can mark the series CANCELLED, send the cancellation email, and return while those events are still on the external calendar; on serverless the continuations are often dropped. Failures are unhandled rejections. Replace the forEach with a for...of or Promise.all and include each deleteEvent promise in apiDeletes before awaiting them.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully
